  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line ltx_leqno">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Huize Jin
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_address"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Address: </span>Academy of Mathematics and Systems Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, China
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email address: </span><a href="mailto:jinhuize@amss.ac.cn">jinhuize@amss.ac.cn</a>
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract.</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We show that the Torelli group of a simply connected closed 5-manifold <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, which is spin and has no 2-torsion elements in homology, is isomorphic to the bordism group <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> with no 2- and 3-torsion we determine this bordism group, and give explicit constructions for the generators of the Torelli group. Furthermore, for the <math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>-fold connected sum <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\#}^{g}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>#</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\#}^{g}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> we completely determine its mapping class group. We apply our results to compute the stabilization and abelianization of the mapping class group of <math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\#}^{g}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>#</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\#}^{g}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>, determine the group of isotopy classes of diffeomorphisms of <math id="abstract1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> that are homotopic to the identity, and study the embeddings of <math id="abstract1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="abstract1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
  
</div>

<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1. </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given a closed oriented smooth manifold <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Diff</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> be the oriented diffeomorphism group of <math id="S1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, equipped with <math id="S1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math>-topology. The <em id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">mapping class group</em> of <math id="S1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>

<p id="S1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">is the group of isotopy classes of orientation preserving diffeomorphisms of <math id="S1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. The subgroup <math id="S1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, consisting of diffeomorphisms that induce the identity homomorphism on <math id="S1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, is called the <em id="S1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Torelli group</em> of <math id="S1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. One may also consider the diffeomorphism group <math id="S1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Diff}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Diff</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Diff}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> and the <em id="S1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">full mapping class group</em></p>

<p id="S1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">consisting of (isotopy classes of) all diffeomorphisms of <math id="S1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover, given a subspace <math id="S1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\subset M</annotation></semantics></math> let <math id="S1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Diff}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Diff</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Diff}(M,D)</annotation></semantics></math> be the group of diffeomorphisms that fix <math id="S1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> pointwise. If <math id="S1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is compact and has nonempty boundary, let <math id="S1.p1.m17" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{Diff}(M,\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Diff</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Diff}(M,\partial)</annotation></semantics></math> be the group of diffeomorphisms that fix some collar neighborhood of the boundary pointwise. There are corresponding versions of relative mapping class groups</p>

<p id="S1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">and relative Torelli groups <math id="S1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,D)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.p1.m19" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,\partial)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Suppose <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is of dimension <math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>. There are several points of view to understand the role of <math id="S1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> in the topology of <math id="S1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. The determination of the mapping class group <math id="S1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is the same as the isotopy classification of orientation preserving diffeomorphisms of <math id="S1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, which is a natural subsequent step to the characterization of the oriented diffeomorphism type of <math id="S1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover, <math id="S1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)=\pi_{0}\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Diff</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)=\pi_{0}\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is the group of path components of <math id="S1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Diff</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> and thus contains homotopic information of <math id="S1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Diff</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Diff}^{+}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, the latter is a major object of interest in geometric topology, and is accessible by methods and techniques from various branches of mathematics (see for example <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kup19</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx53" title="" class="ltx_ref">WW01</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx4" title="" class="ltx_ref">BM20</a>]</cite>). Despite of its significance, a complete description of <math id="S1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> can be hard to achieve. When <math id="S1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is simply connected, the seminal work of Sullivan <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sul77</a>]</cite> implies that <math id="S1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is finitely presentable, so one may have a better chance to compute <math id="S1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> under this assumption.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper we study the mapping class groups of simply connected closed 5-manifolds that are spin and having no 2- and 3-torsion elements in the second homology group. For these manifolds we could compute the Torelli groups explicitly and provide a complete set of concretely constructed generators for these groups. Our main tool is Kreck’s modified surgery theory <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre85</a>]</cite>. We summarize our main results in <a href="#S1.SS1" title="1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a> and sketch our methods in <a href="#S1.SS2" title="1.2. The methods ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.1. </span>The results</h3>

<div id="S1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The primary result of this paper is an explicit computation of Torelli groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion elements in the second homology group. The simplest 5-manifold of such type is <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. By <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordism theorem and Cerf’s pseudoisotopy theorem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cer71</a>, Theorem 1]</cite>, for <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{n})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{n})</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to the Kervaire–Milnor group <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{n+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math> of smooth homotopy spheres, so <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{5})=\Theta_{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{5})=\Theta_{6}</annotation></semantics></math> is trivial. Thus we focus on the case where the second homology of the 5-manifold is nontrivial, since otherwise this manifold is a smooth homotopy sphere which is diffeomorphic to <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> by the fact that <math id="S1.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{5}</annotation></semantics></math> is trivial <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx20" title="" class="ltx_ref">KM63</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 1.1</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S1.ThmDef1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold.</span></p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(1)</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.ix1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.ix1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.ix1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is a short exact sequence</span></p>
<table id="S1.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="S1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We could solve the extension problem in part (1) of Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Therefore we have a complete description of the group structure of <math id="S1.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that if <math id="S1.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> then the linking form vanishes by definition, and <math id="S1.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M_{g}),L_{M_{g}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M_{g}),L_{M_{g}})</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to the general linear group <math id="S1.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<div id="S1.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">

<p id="S1.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">restricting to the identity map on the complement of <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(S^{k}\times D^{n-k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(S^{k}\times D^{n-k})</annotation></semantics></math>, and mapping <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(S^{k}\times D^{n-k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(S^{k}\times D^{n-k})</annotation></semantics></math> to itself by</p>

<p id="S1.SS1.p4.3" class="ltx_p">Clearly the isotopy class of <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on the isotopy class of <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and the homotopy class <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=5</annotation></semantics></math>, the isotopy class of an embedding <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on the isotopy class of the embedding <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S|_{S^{2}\times\{0\}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S|_{S^{2}\times\{0\}}</annotation></semantics></math> of its core sphere (since <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{2}(\mathrm{SO}(3))=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{2}(\mathrm{SO}(3))=0</annotation></semantics></math>) which is determined by its homotopy class by Haefliger’s embedding theorem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hae61</a>]</cite>. Thus, given embeddings <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{1},\cdots,S_{m}:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{1},\cdots,S_{m}:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math>, the embedding <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> with core sphere being the connected sum of the core spheres of <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{1},\cdots,S_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{1},\cdots,S_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> is unique up to isotopy (such a connected sum exists since the codimension is high enough). We denote (the isotopy class of) this embedding by <math id="S1.SS1.p4.m24" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S_{1}\#\cdots\#S_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mi>#</mi><mi>S</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{1}\#\cdots\#S_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S1.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1,\cdots,g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1,\cdots,g</annotation></semantics></math> let <math id="S1.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> be the standard embedding in the <math id="S1.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th <math id="S1.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> summand. Let <math id="S1.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))\cong\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))\cong\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> be the generator such that the first Pontryagin number of the 3-dimensional vector bundle over <math id="S1.SS1.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> with clutching function <math id="S1.SS1.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> is 4.</p>
</div>

<div id="S1.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For example, we can describe <math id="S1.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> as follows. Here the orientation preserving diffeomorphism <math id="S1.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S1.SS1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined by <math id="S1.SS1.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4})\mapsto(-x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},-y_{1},y_{2},y_{3},y_{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation standard embeddings <math id="S1.SS1.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS1.p6.m6" </div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 1.3</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The mapping class group <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z})\rtimes\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋊</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z})\rtimes\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math>, where the action of the nontrivial element of <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> is given by sending an element to its inverse. In other words, <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> has the following presentation:</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by the Dehn twists <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S_{1},\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S_{1},\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S_{1}\#S_{1},\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S_{1}\#S_{1},\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> respectively, and <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>. It follows that <math id="S1.ThmDef3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is residually finite and virtually torsion-free, and has trivial center.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 1.4</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At this point we compare our computation to relevant results in the literature.</p>
<ul id="S1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I2.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(1)</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.ix1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using techniques of pseudoisotopy Sato computed <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{p}\times S^{q})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{p}\times S^{q})</annotation></semantics></math> for certain <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sat69</a>]</cite>. In particular his results imply that there is a splitting exact sequence</p>
<table id="S1.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2\rightarrow 0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2\rightarrow 0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="FC^{3}_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">FC^{3}_{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is Haefliger’s group of isotopy classes of framed 3-knots in <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and is isomorphic to <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hae66</a>, Theorem 5.17]</cite>. Our result extends Sato’s computation of <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> in the sense that we could determine the group structure and provide explicit constructions for generators of <math id="S1.I2.ix1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I2.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(2)</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.ix2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Diffeomorphisms of <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{p}\times S^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{p}\times S^{q}</annotation></semantics></math> have also been considered by Turner <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tur69</a>]</cite> and Levine <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lev69</a>]</cite>. For <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;q&lt;2p-3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;q&lt;2p-3</annotation></semantics></math>, Turner proved that <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(S^{p}\times S^{q})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(S^{p}\times S^{q})</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to a certain semi-direct product <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\pi_{q}(\mathrm{SO}(p+1))\times\Theta_{p+q+1})\rtimes\pi_{p}(\mathrm{SO})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋊</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>SO</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\pi_{q}(\mathrm{SO}(p+1))\times\Theta_{p+q+1})\rtimes\pi_{p}(\mathrm{SO})</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tur69</a>, Theorem 3.10]</cite>. Independently, for <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q&lt;2p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q&lt;2p-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>, Levine <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lev69</a>, Proposition 5.2]</cite> proved that a diffeomorphism of <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{p}\times S^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{p}\times S^{q}</annotation></semantics></math> (not required to be orientation preserving) is pseudoisotopic to a composition of diffeomorphisms of the following three types:</p>
<ul id="S1.I2.ix2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(i)</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,y)\mapsto(\beta(y)\cdot x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,y)\mapsto(\beta(y)\cdot x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta:S^{q}\rightarrow\mathrm{O}(p+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>q</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta:S^{q}\rightarrow\mathrm{O}(p+1)</annotation></semantics></math> is a smooth map;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(ii)</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,y)\mapsto(x,{\beta}^{\prime}(x)\cdot y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,y)\mapsto(x,{\beta}^{\prime}(x)\cdot y)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\beta}^{\prime}:S^{p}\rightarrow\mathrm{O}(q+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\beta}^{\prime}:S^{p}\rightarrow\mathrm{O}(q+1)</annotation></semantics></math> is a smooth map;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(iii)</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">a diffeomorphism supported in an embedded <math id="S1.I2.ix2.I1.ix3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p+q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(p+q)</annotation></semantics></math>-disc.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Note that <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{p}\times S^{p+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{p}\times S^{p+1}</annotation></semantics></math> is included in Turner’s result for <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math> and in Levine’s result for <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Our result shows that <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is not a semi-direct product of such type, and one of its generators, <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S_{1}\#S_{1},\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S_{1}\#S_{1},\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>, cannot be written as such a composition. In this sense <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> differs from <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{p}\times S^{p+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{p}\times S^{p+1}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S1.I2.ix2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I2.ix3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(3)</span> 
<div id="S1.I2.ix3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\#}^{g}(S^{p}\times S^{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>#</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\#}^{g}(S^{p}\times S^{p})</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>, there is an exact sequence</p>
<table id="S1.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is a certain group encoding the action of diffeomorphisms on homology <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre79</a>, Theorem 2]</cite>. For <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> odd this extension problem was studied by Krannich. His result <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kra20</a>, Corollary C]</cite>, which extends earlier results of Crowley <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cro11</a>]</cite> and Galatius–Randal-Williams <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx13" title="" class="ltx_ref">GRW16</a>]</cite>, states that this exact sequence does not split for <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, and splits for <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\neq 3,7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\neq 3,7</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=1</annotation></semantics></math>, when <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=3</annotation></semantics></math> it does not split by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kry03</a>]</cite>, and the case <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=7</annotation></semantics></math> is open. Our result indicates that the behaviors of <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\#}^{g}(S^{p}\times S^{p+1}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>#</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\#}^{g}(S^{p}\times S^{p+1}))</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.I2.ix3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\#}^{g}(S^{p}\times S^{p}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>#</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\#}^{g}(S^{p}\times S^{p}))</annotation></semantics></math> are quite different.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 1.5</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The surjectivity of <math id="S1.ThmDef5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi:\mathrm{MCG}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi:\mathrm{MCG}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})</annotation></semantics></math> in Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a> is due to Barden <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bar65</a>, Theorem 2.2]</cite>. In general no explicit construction for diffeomorphisms which act nontrivially on <math id="S1.ThmDef5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is known (for <math id="S1.ThmDef5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, Trent Lucas has communicated his elegant construction to me). Nonetheless, we show that these diffeomorphisms cannot be Dehn twists (see <a href="#S5.SS5" title="5.5. Diffeomorphisms acting nontrivially on homology are not Dehn twists ‣ 5. Torelli groups of spin 5-manifolds ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Using our computation of <math id="S1.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> we can determine its abelianization.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 1.6</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S1.ThmDef6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<li id="S1.I3.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(1)</span>

<li id="S1.I3.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(2)</span>

</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">In particular oriented smooth fiber bundles with fiber <math id="S1.SS1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> have no 1-dimensional characteristic classes, but may have 2-dimensional characteristic classes of order 2.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Our computation leads to several applications. The first application considers the stable phenomena of diffeomorphisms of 5-manifolds. Namely, there is a well-defined homomorphism <math id="S1.SS1.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M\#(S^{2}\times S^{3}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M\#(S^{2}\times S^{3}))</annotation></semantics></math> induced by taking connected sum with <math id="S1.SS1.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{S^{2}\times S^{3}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{S^{2}\times S^{3}}</annotation></semantics></math> (see Section <a href="#S7" title="7. Stabilization of MCG(𝑀) ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> for details). <p id="S1.SS1.p9.2" class="ltx_p">Two diffeomorphisms are <em id="S1.SS1.p9.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">stably isotopic</em> if they are isotopic after taking connected sums with <math id="S1.SS1.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{S^{2}\times S^{3}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{S^{2}\times S^{3}}</annotation></semantics></math>’s. Our computation implies the following two results.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 1.7</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S1.ThmDef7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with no 2- and 3-torsion elements in homology. Then two orientation preserving diffeomorphisms of <math id="S1.ThmDef7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> are not stably isotopic if they are not isotopic.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 1.8</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The group <math id="S1.ThmDef8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g}))</annotation></semantics></math> stabilizes when <math id="S1.ThmDef8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">As the second application we compare diffeomorphisms and homotopy equivalences of <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. We state a simplified version of our result for <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> and refer to Section <a href="#S8" title="8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> for more general statements. Let <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> be the <em id="S1.SS1.p10.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">homotopy Torelli group</em> of <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, namely the group of homotopy classes of homotopy equivalences of <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> that induce the identity on <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. There is an obvious forgetful homomorphism <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi:\mathcal{I}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi:\mathcal{I}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> be the (smooth) surgery structure set of <math id="S1.SS1.p10.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. <div id="S1.ThmDef9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is an exact sequence (of based sets at <math id="S1.ThmDef9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>, of groups at other terms)</span></p>

<p id="S1.ThmDef9.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef9.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The surgery structure set <math id="S1.ThmDef9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is a finite set containing <math id="S1.ThmDef9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>g</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> elements.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">In particular <math id="S1.SS1.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> consists of all diffeomorphisms of <math id="S1.SS1.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> that are homotopic to <math id="S1.SS1.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M_{g}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M_{g}}</annotation></semantics></math>. More generally, in Section <a href="#S8" title="8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> we compute the group of isotopy classes of diffeomorphisms homotopic to the identity for <math id="S1.SS1.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">As the third application we obtain some information on the problem of which element of <math id="S1.SS1.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by an embedding of <math id="S1.SS1.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S1.SS1.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{1}:S^{2}\hookrightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo <math id="S1.SS1.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1}:S^{3}\hookrightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo
