the standard embeddings, let <math id="S1.SS1.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta:S^{3}\rightarrow S^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" </div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 1.10</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

<div id="S1.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">Given an embedding <math id="S1.SS1.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{\prime}:S^{3}\hookrightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" <div id="S1.ThmDef11" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 1.11</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.ThmDef11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Serre fibration <math id="S1.ThmDef11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Diff}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\rightarrow\mathrm{Emb}(S^{3},S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Diff</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>Emb</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Diff}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\rightarrow\mathrm{Emb}(S^{3},S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is not surjective.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.2. </span>The methods</h3>

<div id="S1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We sketch the method of using modified surgery to study the Torelli group of high-dimensional manifolds. For simplicity we restrict ourselves to the case of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds. Let <math id="S1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be such a manifold. The starting point is to consider the mapping torus</p>

</table>
<p id="S1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">of an orientation preserving diffeomorphism <math id="S1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. This is a closed orientable 6-manifold whose diffeomorphism type is determined by the isotopy class of <math id="S1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<p id="S1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We view <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation f)}(M\times I)</annotation></semantics></math>, namely the result of gluing two copies of <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times I" display="inline" Let <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p:B\rightarrow B\mathrm{SO}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>SO</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p:B\rightarrow B\mathrm{SO}</annotation></semantics></math> be the fibration appearing in the normal <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-type of <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> lies in the relative Torelli group <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi copies of <math id="S1.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">yields a pseudoisotopy between <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>. Cerf’s pseudoisotopy theorem then implies that <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is isotopic to <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math>. All these diffeomrphisms and isotopies could be made to fix the disc <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> pointwise. In our case we could show that <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is a homomorphism, thus it is injective.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Kreck–Su’s observation suggests investigating the bordism group <math id="S1.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{6}(B,p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{6}(B,p)</annotation></semantics></math>. We compute this group and determine the relevant bordism invariants using Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence. When <math id="S1.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> has no 2-torsion elements this bordism group has no 2-torsion either, so Wall’s exact sequence (<a href="#S1.Ex26" title="1.2. The methods ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a>) implies that <math id="S1.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)=\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,D)=\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S1.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, we calculate the bordism invariants for the mapping tori of certain Dehn twists using explicit geometric methods, where the Hopf invariant plays a fundamental role. This leads to the determination of <math id="S1.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> and its generators.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Based on the determination of <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> we could compute <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. Using modified surgery we show that <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)</annotation></semantics></math>, the relative mapping class group of the <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>-fold boundary connected sum of <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times D^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times D^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, is isomorphic to <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. Barden’s result <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bar65</a>, Theorem 2.3]</cite> implies that <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is a twisted double of <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> for certain <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, so there is a homomorphism <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> induced by extending a diffeomorphism by identity. The computation of <math id="S1.SS2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> and the determination of its generators result from analyzing this homomorphism using bordism groups and spectral sequences.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The major advantage of this modified surgery approach is that it enables us to define isotopy invariants for diffeomorphisms in the Torelli group, in terms of certain differential topological invariants (in our case, bordism invariants) of their mapping tori. (For a similar but more complicated result for certain 6-manifolds, making use of the Kreck–Stolz invariants for certain 7-manifolds, see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx27" title="" class="ltx_ref">KS25</a>]</cite>.) These invariants, or more generally, considering the bordism properties of mapping tori, converts the isotopy classification of diffeomorphisms into bordism theoretic constructions and differential topological calculations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.ThmDef12" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.ThmDef12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 1.12</span></span><span id="S1.ThmDef12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.ThmDef12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.ThmDef12.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The modified surgery approach described in this subsection applies to non-spin 5-manifolds after mild modification (compare <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx27" title="" class="ltx_ref">KS25</a>, Section 10]</cite>). Moreover one may use this approach to study the mapping class groups of closed <math id="S1.ThmDef12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(4q+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4q+1)</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional manifolds (see the statement of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Theorem 5]</cite>).</p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.3. </span>Structure of the paper</h3>

<div id="S1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Section <a href="#S2" title="2. The mapping torus construction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> we define the map <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>. Section <a href="#S3" title="3. The spin bordism groups of certain Eilenberg–MacLane spaces ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> is devoted to the determination of relevant bordism groups and their bordism invariants. In Section <a href="#S4" title="4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> we compute <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. In Section <a href="#S5" title="5. Torelli groups of spin 5-manifolds ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> we prove Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a>, completing our computation of Torelli groups. In Section <a href="#S6" title="6. The mapping class group of 𝑀_𝑔 and its abelianization ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> we show that <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is a semi-direct product by a bordism theoretic construction, completing the proof of Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef2" title="Theorem 1.2. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a>, and compute the abelianization of <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. The study of stabilization of <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is contained in Section <a href="#S7" title="7. Stabilization of MCG(𝑀) ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. The comparison to homotopy equivalences of <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is contained in Section <a href="#S8" title="8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>. Finally we prove Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef10" title="Theorem 1.10. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.10</span></a> and Corollary <a href="#S1.ThmDef11" title="Corollary 1.11. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.11</span></a> in Section <a href="#S9" title="9. Embeddings of 𝑆^3 in 𝑆^2×𝑆^3 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2. </span>The mapping torus construction</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed oriented 5-manifold, <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> be a diffeomorphism of <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> acting trivially on <math id="S2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> be the mapping torus of <math id="S2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>. We denote the inclusion <math id="S2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=M\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}\hookrightarrow M_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=M\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}\hookrightarrow M_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. The Wang sequence of the fibration <math id="S2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\xrightarrow{i}M_{f}\rightarrow S^{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝑖</mo></mover><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\xrightarrow{i}M_{f}\rightarrow S^{1}</annotation></semantics></math> implies that <math id="S2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i^{*}:H^{2}(M_{f};\mathbb{Z}/2)\rightarrow H^{2}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i^{*}:H^{2}(M_{f};\mathbb{Z}/2)\rightarrow H^{2}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{*}:H_{2}(M)\rightarrow H_{2}(M_{f})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{*}:H_{2}(M)\rightarrow H_{2}(M_{f})</annotation></semantics></math> are isomorphisms. In particular <math id="S2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> is spin if and only if <math id="S2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is spin, since <math id="S2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i^{*}w_{2}(M_{f})=w_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i^{*}w_{2}(M_{f})=w_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">From now on we assume <math id="S2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is spin. We will need the notion of <em id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">normal <math id="S2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-type</em>, for the definition we refer to <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>]</cite>. The normal <math id="S2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-type of <math id="S2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>

<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Now choose an embedded 5-disc <math id="S2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\subset M</annotation></semantics></math> and suppose <math id="S2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> represents an element of <math id="S2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,D)</annotation></semantics></math>. There is an embedded submanifold <math id="S2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{1}\times D\subset M_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{1}\times D\subset M_{f}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{\mathrm{Spin}}:M_{f}\rightarrow B\mathrm{Spin}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>Spin</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Spin</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{\mathrm{Spin}}:M_{f}\rightarrow B\mathrm{Spin}</annotation></semantics></math> be the classifying map of the preferred spin structure lifting the normal Gauss map of <math id="S2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{f}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{f}:M_{f}\rightarrow K(H_{2}(M),2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{f}:M_{f}\rightarrow K(H_{2}(M),2)</annotation></semantics></math> be a map inducing <math id="S2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{*}^{-1}:H_{2}(M_{f})\rightarrow H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{*}^{-1}:H_{2}(M_{f})\rightarrow H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, which is unique up to homotopy. The map</p>

<div id="S2.ThmDef1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.ThmDef1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2.1</span></span><span id="S2.ThmDef1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.ThmDef1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.ThmDef1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.ThmDef1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The mapping torus construction <math id="S2.ThmDef1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is an injective homomorphism.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">First we show that <math id="S2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is a homomorphism. Let <math id="S2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[f],[f^{\prime}]\in\mathcal{I}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[f],[f^{\prime}]\in\mathcal{I}(M,D)</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> be the compact smooth manifold obtained from <math id="S2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times I\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times I\times I</annotation></semantics></math> by identifying <math id="S2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times\{0\}\times[0,1/3]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times\{0\}\times[0,1/3]</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times\{0\}\times[2/3,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times\{0\}\times[2/3,1]</annotation></semantics></math> via</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<math id="S2.p5.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math> can be chosen so that it also extends <math id="S2.p5.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ν</mi><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p5.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu_{f\circ f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ν</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu_{f\circ f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Now <math id="S2.p5.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(W,\widetilde{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W,\widetilde{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math> is a normal <math id="S2.p5.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-bordism between <math id="S2.p5.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M_{f},\overline{\nu})\sqcup(M_{f^{\prime}},\overline{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M_{f},\overline{\nu})\sqcup(M_{f^{\prime}},\overline{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p5.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M_{f\circ f^{\prime}},\overline{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M_{f\circ f^{\prime}},\overline{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math>, thus <math id="S2.p5.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho([f])+\rho([f^{\prime}])=\rho([f\circ f^{\prime}])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho([f])+\rho([f^{\prime}])=\rho([f\circ f^{\prime}])</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Then we show that <math id="S2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is injective. Suppose <math id="S2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[M_{f},\overline{\nu}]=0\in\Omega_{6}(B,p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[M_{f},\overline{\nu}]=0\in\Omega_{6}(B,p)</annotation></semantics></math>. Choose a coboundary <math id="S2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(W,\widetilde{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W,\widetilde{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M_{f},\overline{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M_{f},\overline{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math>. View it as a normal <math id="S2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-bordism, relative to boundary, between <math id="S2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times I</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times I</annotation></semantics></math>. By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Theorems 4 and 5]</cite>, the modified surgery obstruction of <math id="S2.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(W,\widetilde{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W,\widetilde{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math> is elementary, thus there is another coboundary of <math id="S2.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M_{f},\overline{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M_{f},\overline{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math>, which is an <math id="S2.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordism relative to boundary. We still denote this coboundary by <math id="S2.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math>. By <math id="S2.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordism theorem we have a diffeomorphism <math id="S2.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W\cong M\times I\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W\cong M\times I\times I</annotation></semantics></math>. The embedding <math id="S2.p6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{1}\times D\hookrightarrow M_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{1}\times D\hookrightarrow M_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> extends to an embedding <math id="S2.p6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{2}\times D\hookrightarrow W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{2}\times D\hookrightarrow W</annotation></semantics></math>, which is an <math id="S2.p6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordism between <math id="S2.p6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\times I</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\times I</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S2.p6.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> (and <math id="S2.p6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\setminus D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∖</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\setminus D</annotation></semantics></math>) is simply connected, by relative <math id="S2.p6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordism theorem there is a dffeomorphism <math id="S2.p6.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times I\rightarrow M\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times I\rightarrow M\times I</annotation></semantics></math> extending <math id="S2.p6.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id:D\times I\rightarrow D\times I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id:D\times I\rightarrow D\times I</annotation></semantics></math>, restricting to <math id="S2.p6.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p6.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times\{0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times\{0\}</annotation></semantics></math> and restricting to <math id="S2.p6.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p6.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\times\{1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\times\{1\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus <math id="S2.p6.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f|_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f|_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}</annotation></semantics></math> is pseudoisotopic, relative to boundary, to <math id="S2.p6.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Cerf’s pseudoisotopy theorem implies that <math id="S2.p6.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f|_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f|_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}</annotation></semantics></math> is isotopic, relative to boundary, to <math id="S2.p6.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M\setminus\mathring{D}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Gluing <math id="S2.p6.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> back we obtain an isotopy between <math id="S2.p6.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p6.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math>, fixing <math id="S2.p6.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> pointwise. So <math id="S2.p6.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[f]=[id_{M}]\in\mathcal{I}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[f]=[id_{M}]\in\mathcal{I}(M,D)</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore <math id="S2.p6.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is injective.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The forgetful homomorphism <math id="S2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M,D)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M,D)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, which restricts to <math id="S2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,D)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, is surjective by the disc theorem and isotopy extension theorem. We have the following result of Wall <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wal63a</a>, page 265]</cite> concerning the kernel of this homomorphism.</p>
</div>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.ThmDef2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2.2</span></span><span id="S2.ThmDef2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Wall)<span id="S2.ThmDef2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.ThmDef2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.ThmDef2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.ThmDef2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.ThmDef2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected oriented <math id="S2.ThmDef2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold with <math id="S2.ThmDef2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.ThmDef2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\subset M</annotation></semantics></math> be an embedded <math id="S2.ThmDef2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-disc. <td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex39.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mapsto(\beta(t)\cdot x,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mapsto(\beta(t)\cdot x,t)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p8.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p8.3.1" class="ltx_text">and extend it to a diffeomorphism of <math id="S2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> by identity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre79</a>, page 657]</cite>. Clearly this relative isotopy class lies in <math id="S2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,D)</annotation></semantics></math>, so we obtain the exact sequence in the second row.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3. </span>The spin bordism groups of certain Eilenberg–MacLane spaces</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In light of Lemma <a href="#S2.ThmDef1" title="Lemma 2.1. ‣ 2. The mapping torus construction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> we study the bordism group <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold. For <math id="S3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> having no 2- and 3-torsion we could determine the isomorphism type and the bordism invariants of this bordism group. We also study a certain homomorphism between these groups induced by the quotient homomorphism.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1. </span>Low-dimensional homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">First we recall the low-dimensional integral homology groups of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is a prime number and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is a positive integer. The cases of dimension <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 6</annotation></semantics></math> were determined by Eilenberg and MacLane in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx11" title="" class="ltx_ref">EM54</a>, Chapter IV]</cite>. The 7-dimensional homology group appears to be much more difficult to investigate using their methods (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx11" title="" class="ltx_ref">EM54</a>, page 116]</cite>). We compute this group using the Leray–Serre spectral sequence of the homotopy fibration <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},1)\rightarrow*\rightarrow K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>K</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},1)\rightarrow*\rightarrow K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2)</annotation></semantics></math> and the mod <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> cohomology of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},n)</annotation></semantics></math>, the latter was determined by Cartan <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Car55</a>]</cite> for <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math> and by Serre <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ser53</a>]</cite> for <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math>. Precisely, for <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\neq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\neq 2</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> the spectral sequence and the integral homology of dimension <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 6</annotation></semantics></math> implies that the 7-dimensional homology is trivial. For <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>, the spectral sequence implies that the 7-dimensional homology is a finite abelian group which is either trivial or <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/p</annotation></semantics></math>, and the mod <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> cohomology tells us that it is <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/{p^{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/{p^{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, hence it is <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/p</annotation></semantics></math>. In summary we have the following.</p>
</div>

<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2. </span>Computation of <math id="S3.SS2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence to determine <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> and its bordism invariants, which are, informally speaking, given by (the Poincaré dual of) the first Pontryagin class and the fundamental class. The low-dimensional spin cobordism groups <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>∗</mo><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{*}</annotation></semantics></math> are as follows <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mil63</a>]</cite>.</p>

<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We shall consider two special cases, namely <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, before dealing with the general case. We consider <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> first. Let <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{k}\in H^{2}({(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{k}\in H^{2}({(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g})</annotation></semantics></math> be the Kronecker dual of the generator <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\mathbb{CP}}^{1}]_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[{\mathbb{CP}}^{1}]_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> corresponding to the <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{CP}}^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{CP}}^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> factor. Then <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{6}({({\mathbb{CP}}^{\infty})}^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{6}({({\mathbb{CP}}^{\infty})}^{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is a free abelian group of rank <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g+2{\binom{g}{2}}+{\binom{g}{3}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>g</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g+2{\binom{g}{2}}+{\binom{g}{3}}</annotation></semantics></math>, generated by the Kronecker duals</p>

<p id="S3.SS2.p3.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p3.4.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\hat{A}_{k})\coloneqq(\hat{A}_{1},\cdots,\hat{A}_{g}):A\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>g</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\hat{A}_{k})\coloneqq(\hat{A}_{1},\cdots,\hat{A}_{g}):A\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is surjective. Thus <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}\rightarrow{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}\rightarrow{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is an isomorphism. By 5-lemma <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\hat{A}_{k}):A\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\hat{A}_{k}):A\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is an isomorphism.
∎</span></p>

<p id="S3.SS2.p7.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p7.6.1" class="ltx_text">The proofs of Proposition <a href="#S3.ThmDef1" title="Proposition 3.1. ‣ 3.2. Computation of Ω^Spin_6⁢(𝐾(𝐻_2⁢(𝑀),2)) ‣ 3. The spin bordism groups of certain Eilenberg–MacLane spaces ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> and Proposition <a href="#S3.ThmDef2" title="Proposition 3.2. ‣ 3.2. Computation of Ω^Spin_6⁢(𝐾(𝐻_2⁢(𝑀),2)) ‣ 3. The spin bordism groups of certain Eilenberg–MacLane spaces ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> assemble to show that <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is surjective, thus <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}\rightarrow{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}\rightarrow{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is an isomorphism. By 5-lemma <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau:A_{M}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^{g}\oplus T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo>⊕</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau:A_{M}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^{g}\oplus T</annotation></semantics></math> is an isomorphism. Thus there is a commutative diagram</span></p>

<p id="S3.SS2.p7.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p7.8.1" class="ltx_text">As in the proof of Proposition <a href="#S3.ThmDef1" title="Proposition 3.1. ‣ 3.2. The exact sequence</span></p>

<div id="S3.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Thus the bordism group <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> is abstractly isomorphic to <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)\oplus H_{M}\cong H_{2}(M)\oplus H_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo
