id="S3.SS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> has no 2- and 3-torsion. This group can be calculated using Künneth theorem, so the isomorphism type of <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> is explicitly determined (see <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3. Generators of ℐ(𝑀) ‣ 5. Torelli groups of spin 5-manifolds ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>). When <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> contains nontrivial 2- or 3-torsion, the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence is more complicated and the computation of <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> will be considered in a subsequent paper.</p>

<div id="S3.ThmDef4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.ThmDef4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3.4</span></span><span id="S3.ThmDef4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.ThmDef4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.ThmDef4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.ThmDef4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.ThmDef4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with no 2-torsion in homology, then <math id="S3.ThmDef4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M,D)=\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M,D)=\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.ThmDef4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)=\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,D)=\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.SS2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">The bordism group <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> has no 2-torsion. So is <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M,D)</annotation></semantics></math> since it can be viewed as a subgroup of <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> via <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math>. The corollary follows from Lemma <a href="#S2.ThmDef2" title="Lemma 2.2 (Wall). ‣ 2. The mapping torus construction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> since <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{1}(\mathrm{SO}(5))\cong\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{1}(\mathrm{SO}(5))\cong\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>

stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation alttext="*=4,6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" The canonical generator of <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{4}(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{4}(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is mapped by <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{*}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}}=H_{4}(K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2))" display="inline" alttext="\ell^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{4}(K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2);\mathbb{Z}/p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo Thus <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=m+kp" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=m+kp</annotation></semantics></math> for some integer <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k,m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k,m</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq m\leq p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq m\leq p-1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is coprime to <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p^{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p^{r}</annotation></semantics></math> and hence is a generator of <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{4}(K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{4}(K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2))</annotation></semantics></math>. Similarly we see that <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{*}:H_{6}(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})\rightarrow H_{6}(K(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}},2))" display="inline" ∎</span></p>

<div id="S3.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In general <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta:{(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g+2s}\rightarrow K(H,2)" display="inline" <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id:\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}\rightarrow\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" Using this fact we can prove the following.</p>

<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span>The Torelli group of <math id="S4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math></h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>-fold connected sum <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\#}^{g}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>#</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\#}^{g}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>. In this section we show that the map <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho:\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rightarrow\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}({(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho:\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rightarrow\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}({(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g})</annotation></semantics></math> given by Corollary <a href="#S3.ThmDef4" title="Corollary 3.4. ‣ 3.2. Computation of Ω^Spin_6⁢(𝐾(𝐻_2⁢(𝑀),2)) ‣ 3. The spin bordism groups of certain Eilenberg–MacLane spaces ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a> is an isomorphism. More precisely, (the isotopy classes of) the Dehn twists listed in Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef2" title="Theorem 1.2. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a> are in <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> by the following Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef1" title="Lemma 4.1. ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, and we show that these Dehn twists are mapped to a basis of <math id="S4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}({(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}({(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g})</annotation></semantics></math>, by calculating the bordism invariants of their mapping torus constructions by explicit geometric considerations. As a byproduct we determine the action of <math id="S4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.ThmDef1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4.1</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.ThmDef1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.ThmDef1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.ThmDef1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.ThmDef1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math> be an embedding in a simply connected closed 5-manifold <math id="S4.ThmDef1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S4.ThmDef1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))</annotation></semantics></math>. Then the Dehn twist <math id="S4.ThmDef1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> acts trivially on <math id="S4.ThmDef1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Clearly <math id="S4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> preserves the orientation of <math id="S4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. By Hurewicz theorem and Whitney’s embedding theorem we may assume <math id="S4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)=\pi_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)=\pi_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is generated by embeddings of <math id="S4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, which by transversality are disjoint with the image of <math id="S4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>, and thus are fixed by <math id="S4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence <math id="S4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> acts trivially on <math id="S4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, and therefore acts trivially on <math id="S4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> by Poincaré duality.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1. </span>The first Pontryagin class</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">First we calculate <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle p_{1}({(M_{g})}_{f})\cup{{\nu}_{f}}^{*}(x_{k}),[{(M_{g})}_{f}]\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>ν</mi><mi>f</mi><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle p_{1}({(M_{g})}_{f})\cup{{\nu}_{f}}^{*}(x_{k}),[{(M_{g})}_{f}]\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is a Dehn twist about an embedding of <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times D^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times D^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. We shall need the following geometric observation which is an analogue of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx27" title="" class="ltx_ref">KS25</a>, Lemma 7.11]</cite>. The proof is evident.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.ThmDef2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4.2</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.ThmDef2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S:S^{2}\times D^{3}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math> be an embedding in a closed 5-manifold <math id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> be the Dehn twist about <math id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.ThmDef2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>. <p id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where </span><math id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi:S^{2}\times S^{3}\rightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi:S^{2}\times S^{3}\rightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is given by </span><math id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,y)\mapsto(\beta(y)\cdot x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,y)\mapsto(\beta(y)\cdot x,y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>

<li id="S4.I1.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(2)</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.ix2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{\beta}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> be the 3-dimensional vector bundle over </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{4}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> with clutching function </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">. Let </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D(\xi_{\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(\xi_{\beta})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> denotes the total space of the associated unit disc bundle, and </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial D(\xi_{\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial D(\xi_{\beta})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> denotes the total space of the associated unit sphere bundle. Then </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\partial D(\xi_{\beta})=(S^{2}\times D^{4})\cup_{\varphi}(S^{2}\times D^{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>∪</mo><mi>φ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial D(\xi_{\beta})=(S^{2}\times D^{4})\cup_{\varphi}(S^{2}\times D^{4})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}=\partial((M\times D^{2})\cup_{S^{2}\times D^{4}}D(\xi_{\beta}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>∪</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}=\partial((M\times D^{2})\cup_{S^{2}\times D^{4}}D(\xi_{\beta}))</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>

<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Denote the oriented manifold <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(M_{g}\times D^{2})\cup_{S^{2}\times D^{4}}D(\xi_{\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>∪</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M_{g}\times D^{2})\cup_{S^{2}\times D^{4}}D(\xi_{\beta})</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> so that <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}=\partial W_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}=\partial W_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math>. The Mayer–Vietoris sequence implies that <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{4}(W_{S,\beta})\cong\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{4}(W_{S,\beta})\cong\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>, and it is generated by the fundamental class <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[S^{4}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[S^{4}]</annotation></semantics></math> of the base of the bundle <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> (realized as the zero section of <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{\beta}</annotation></semantics></math>, thus a submanifold of <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D(\xi_{\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(\xi_{\beta})</annotation></semantics></math>), and there is an exact sequence</p>

<p id="S4.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the inclusion map. alttext="[S^{4}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation alttext="i_{*}S_{*}([S^{2}])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" In fact the ambiguous sign “<math id="S4.SS1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>” can be removed.</p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4.3</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.ThmDef3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.ThmDef3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.ThmDef3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Poincaré dual of <math id="S4.ThmDef3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{*}S_{*}([S^{2}])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{*}S_{*}([S^{2}])</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S4.ThmDef3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j^{*}({[S^{4}]}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j^{*}({[S^{4}]}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<p id="S4.SS1.p3.3" class="ltx_p">since <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{*}(W_{S,\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{*}(W_{S,\beta})</annotation></semantics></math> has no 2-torsion. Thus</p>
<table id="S4.Ex102" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex102.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}({(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}})=j^{*}(p_{1}(W_{S,\beta}))=4nj^{*}({[S^{4}]}^{*})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}({(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}})=j^{*}(p_{1}(W_{S,\beta}))=4nj^{*}({[S^{4}]}^{*}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.4" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\nu}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}}^{*}(x_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>ν</mi><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\nu}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}}^{*}(x_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> is the Kronecker dual of <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{*}{S_{k}}_{*}([S^{2}])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{*}{S_{k}}_{*}([S^{2}])</annotation></semantics></math>, Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef3" title="Lemma 4.3. ‣ 4.1. The first Pontryagin class ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> implies the following.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.ThmDef4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4.4</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.ThmDef4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.ThmDef4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.ThmDef4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S4.ThmDef4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.ThmDef4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> as above and for each <math id="S4.ThmDef4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>

<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Finally we prove Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef3" title="Lemma 4.3. ‣ 4.1. The first Pontryagin class ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> and thus complete the calculation of the Pontryagin class.</p>

<div id="S4.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef3" title="Lemma 4.3. ‣ 4.1. The first Pontryagin class ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="S4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Still suppose <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[S]=d_{1}[S_{1}]+\cdots+d_{g}[S_{g}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[S]=d_{1}[S_{1}]+\cdots+d_{g}[S_{g}]</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that the embedding <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell:S^{2}=S^{2}\times\{*\}\hookrightarrow S^{2}\times D^{4}\hookrightarrow{(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}" display="inline" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell:S^{2}=S^{2}\times\{*\}\hookrightarrow S^{2}\times D^{4}\hookrightarrow{(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}</annotation></semantics></math> is isotopic to <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\circ S" display="inline" <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\ell}_{*}([S^{2}])=\sum_{k=1}^{g}d_{k}i_{*}{S_{k}}_{*}([S^{2}])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo By a well-known result of Thom <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tho54</a>, Theorem II. 27]</cite>, the Poincaré dual of <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\nu}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}}^{*}(x_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>ν</mi><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\nu}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}}^{*}(x_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by the fundamental class of a 4-dimensional closed submanifold <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}\subset{(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}\subset{(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}}</annotation></semantics></math> for each <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>. The intersection number of submanifolds <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(S^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(S^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> extends to an embedding <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\ell}:D^{3}\hookrightarrow D(\xi_{\beta})\hookrightarrow W_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\ell}:D^{3}\hookrightarrow D(\xi_{\beta})\hookrightarrow W_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> of a fiber of the unit disc bundle. Using a collar neighborhood we may isotope <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> into the interior of <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> and obtain a closed submanifold <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}^{\prime}\subset W_{S,\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}^{\prime}\subset W_{S,\beta}</annotation></semantics></math>, whose fundamental class represents <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{*}([N_{k}])\in H_{4}(W_{S,\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>j</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{*}([N_{k}])\in H_{4}(W_{S,\beta})</annotation></semantics></math>. Then the intersection number of <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\ell}(D^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\ell}(D^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. The intersection number of <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\ell}(D^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo alttext="S^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is 1, so <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\overline{\ell}}_{*}([D^{3},S^{2}])\in H_{3}(W_{S,\beta},{(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\beta}})" display="inline" <section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2. </span>The cubic form</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this subsection we calculate the cubic form on <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{2}({(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\alpha}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{2}({(M_{g})}_{\mathbf{t}_{S,\alpha}})</annotation></semantics></math> induced by cup product, where <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{t}_{S,\alpha}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{t}_{S,\alpha}}</annotation></semantics></math> is one of the Dehn twists listed in Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef2" title="Theorem 1.2. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a>. We begin by sketching the strategy to make the calculation a bit more transparent. A diffeomorphism of <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> is homotopic to a cellular map and we denote by <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> its restriction on the 3-skeleton <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∨</mo><mi>g</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. The map <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> acts trivially on <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H_{*}(\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em">∨</mo><mi>g</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))</annotation></semantics></math> if the original diffeomorphism acts trivially on <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. The CW structure of the mapping torus <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em">∨</mo><mi>g</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))_{f}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is determined by the action of <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\pi_{3}(\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em">∨</mo><mi>g</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))</annotation></semantics></math>, enables us to calculate the cup product</p>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.1. </span>Action of Dehn twists on <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math></h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1,\cdots,g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1,\cdots,g</annotation></semantics></math> let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{k}:S^{3}\hookrightarrow M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{k}:S^{3}\hookrightarrow M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> be the standard embedding of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> in the <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> summand. The homotopy group</p>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Using Whitney trick we may assume <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(S^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(S^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> intersect at <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> points transversally. encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> given by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\mapsto\frac{1}{4}\langle <div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Now we determine the action of the Dehn twists listed in Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef2" title="Theorem 1.2. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a> on <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. It suffices to determine their actions on <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[T_{1}],\cdots,[T_{g}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[T_{1}],\cdots,[T_{g}]</annotation></semantics></math>. By Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef5" title="Lemma 4.5. ‣ 4.2.1. Action of Dehn twists on 𝜋_3⁢(𝑀_𝑔) ‣ 4.2. The cubic form ‣ 4. <div id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Consider the embedding <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="({\#}^{d_{1}}S_{1})\#\cdots\#({\#}^{d_{g}}S_{g}):S^{2}\hookrightarrow M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>#</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msup><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mi>#</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>#</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msup><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">({\#}^{d_{1}}S_{1})\#\cdots\#({\#}^{d_{g}}S_{g}):S^{2}\hookrightarrow M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>. We calculate the homotopy class <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[\bigl(({\#}^{d_{1}}S_{1})\#\cdots\#({\#}^{d_{g}}S_{g})\bigr)\circ\eta]\in\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>#</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msup><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mi>#</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>#</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></msup><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\bigl(({\#}^{d_{1}}S_{1})\#\cdots\#({\#}^{d_{g}}S_{g})\bigr)\circ\eta]\in\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> using (the geometric interpretation of) Hopf invariant. <p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the map collapsing the complement of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{k}(S^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{k}(S^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> into a point, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the map collapsing the corresponding discs into a point. Note that <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is homotopic to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{S^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{S^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since the induced homomorphism <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m14" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{q_{k}}_{*}:\pi_{3}(\vee_{d}S^{2})\rightarrow\pi_{3}(S^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em">∨</mo><mi>d</mi></msub><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{q_{k}}_{*}:\pi_{3}(\vee_{d}S^{2})\rightarrow\pi_{3}(S^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> maps <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[i_{k}\circ\eta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[i_{k}\circ\eta]</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\eta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\eta]</annotation></semantics></math> and maps other generators to zero, by the commutative diagram we have <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{k}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{k}=1</annotation></semantics></math> for each <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>. <p id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{k,l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{k,l}</annotation></semantics></math> is the map collapsing the complement of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{k}(S^{2})\vee i_{l}(S^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{k}(S^{2})\vee i_{l}(S^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> into a point, and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k,l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k,l}</annotation></semantics></math> is the map collapsing the corresponding discs into a point. We note that <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k,l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k,l}</annotation></semantics></math> is homotopic to the quotient map <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{2}:S^{2}\rightarrow S^{2}\vee S^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{2}:S^{2}\rightarrow S^{2}\vee S^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The induced homomorphism <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m25" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{q_{k,l}}_{*}:\pi_{3}(\vee_{d}S^{2})\rightarrow\pi_{3}(S^{2}\vee S^{2})" display="inline" alttext="[\pi_{d}\circ\eta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" Using the aforementioned geometric interpretation, we see that the Hopf invariant of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m30" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[(\vee_{d}id)\circ\pi_{d}\circ\eta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em">∨</mo><mi>d</mi></msub><mi>i</mi><mi>d</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[(\vee_{d}id)\circ\pi_{d}\circ\eta]</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, thus <math id="S4.SS2.SSS1.p6.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[(id\vee id)\circ\pi_{2}\circ\eta]=4[\eta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[(id\vee id)\circ\pi_{2}\circ\eta]=4[\eta]</annotation></semantics></math>. <section id="S4.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.2. </span>The cup product of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H^{*}((\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))_{f})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mo lspace="0em">∨</mo><mi>g</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{*}((\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3}))_{f})</annotation></semantics></math></h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For brevity we denote <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∨</mo><mi>g</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\vee_{g}(S^{2}\vee S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{k}:S^{2}\hookrightarrow V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{k}:S^{2}\hookrightarrow V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> be the inclusion of the <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th copy of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{k}:S^{3}\hookrightarrow V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>j</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{k}:S^{3}\hookrightarrow V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> be the inclusion of the <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th copy of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. If we view <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> as the 3-skeleton of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> then <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i_{k}\simeq S_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≃</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i_{k}\simeq S_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j_{k}\simeq T_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>j</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≃</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j_{k}\simeq T_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. <div id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We summarize these calculations into a lemma.</p>

<div id="S4.ThmDef7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4.7</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
