<section id="S4.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.2.3. </span>Determination of the cubic form</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> be a diffeomorphism of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> acting trivially on homology, and let <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> be a cellular map homotopic to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then the mapping tori <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(M_{g})}_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(M_{g})}_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> are homotopy equivalent relative to the subspace <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}</annotation></semantics></math> (see for example <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hat02</a>, Proposition 0.18]</cite>). Such a homotopy equivalence commutes with the inclusion maps <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}=M_{g}\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}\hookrightarrow{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}=M_{g}\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}\hookrightarrow{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}=M_{g}\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}\hookrightarrow{(M_{g})}_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}=M_{g}\times\{\frac{1}{2}\}\hookrightarrow{(M_{g})}_{f}</annotation></semantics></math>. We identify the (co)homology groups of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(M_{g})}_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(M_{g})}_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> via the induced isomorphisms of such a homotopy equivalence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the 3-skeleton of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, and we still denote the restriction of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:V_{g}\rightarrow V_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f:V_{g}\rightarrow V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. The mapping torus <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(V_{g})}_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(V_{g})}_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> is a subcomplex of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(M_{g})}_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(M_{g})}_{f}</annotation></semantics></math>. Using the Wang sequence for mapping tori <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hat02</a>, Example 2.48]</cite>, we see that the inclusion map <math stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(V_{g})}_{f}\hookrightarrow{(M_{g})}_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> induces isomorphisms on (co)homology groups of dimension up to 4, and moreover, it maps the homology class <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{i_{k}}_{*}([S^{2}])=[S^{2}_{k}]\in H_{2}({(V_{g})}_{f})" display="inline" <p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.4" class="ltx_p">By the construction of Wang sequence we see that <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial[e^{4}_{k}]=[S^{3}_{k}]\in H_{3}(V_{g})=H_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mphantom></mphantom><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial[e^{4}_{k}]=[S^{3}_{k}]\in H_{3}(V_{g})=H_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. The homology class <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial[N_{k}]\in H_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mphantom></mphantom><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial[N_{k}]\in H_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is represented by the following 3-dimensional submanifold: there is a 4-dimensional submanifold of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}\times I" display="inline" I</annotation></semantics></math> with boundary, denoted by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{N}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{N}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is mapped to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> by the quotient map <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}\times I\rightarrow{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}\times I\rightarrow{(M_{g})}_{f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> represents the Poincaré dual of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\nu_{f^{\prime}}}^{*}(x_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>ν</mi><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\nu_{f^{\prime}}}^{*}(x_{k})</annotation></semantics></math>, the intersection number of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is 1, thus <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}\cap(M_{g}\times\{t\})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}\cap(M_{g}\times\{t\})</annotation></semantics></math> is nonempty for each <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Denote the boundary component <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{N}_{k}\cap(M_{g}\times\{0\})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{N}_{k}\cap(M_{g}\times\{0\})</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is a 3-dimensional closed submanifold of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. The fundamental class of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial[N_{k}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial[N_{k}]</annotation></semantics></math>. The intersection number of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}_{k}" display="inline" <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p2.m42" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}_{l}" display="inline" <p id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These isomorphisms are induced by maps between spaces and thus preserve the cup product structure. Therefore the cubic form on <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{2}({(M_{g})}_{f})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{2}({(M_{g})}_{f})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS2.SSS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is a Dehn twist listed in Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef2" title="Theorem 1.2. ‣ 1.1. <div id="S4.ThmDef8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4.8</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.ThmDef8.p1" class="ltx_para">

<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3. </span>The group <math id="S4.SS3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The bordism invariants of the mapping tori of the Dehn twists listed in Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef2" title="Theorem 1.2. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a> are determined by Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef4" title="Lemma 4.4. ‣ 4.1. The first Pontryagin class ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a> and Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef8" title="Lemma 4.8. ‣ 4.2.3. Determination of the cubic form ‣ 4.2. The cubic form ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.8</span></a>. The result shows that the mapping torus constructions of these Dehn twists form a basis of <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})</annotation></semantics></math>, thus <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho:\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rightarrow{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho:\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rightarrow{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is an isomorphism and these Dehn twists form a basis of <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. We list the values of the bordism invariants for <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\leq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\leq 3</annotation></semantics></math> below, and summarize the results of this section into the following theorem. To simplify the notation, we write <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{x}_{k}^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{x}_{k}^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> for the evaluation of <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\nu_{f}}^{*}(x_{k}^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>ν</mi><mi>f</mi><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\nu_{f}}^{*}(x_{k}^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> on the fundamental class of the mapping torus (and the other notations should be interpreted similarly), and <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\overline{x}_{k}^{2}\overline{x}_{l})^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\overline{x}_{k}^{2}\overline{x}_{l})^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> stands for <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{2}(\overline{x}_{k}^{2}\overline{x}_{l}-\overline{x}_{k}\overline{x}_{l}^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(\overline{x}_{k}^{2}\overline{x}_{l}-\overline{x}_{k}\overline{x}_{l}^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

<div id="S4.ThmDef9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.9</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.ThmDef9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.ThmDef9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.ThmDef9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S4.ThmDef9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> the mapping torus construction <math id="S4.ThmDef9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho:\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rightarrow{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho:\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rightarrow{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is an isomorphism, thus <math id="S4.ThmDef9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S4.ThmDef9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}^{2g+2{\binom{g}{2}}+{\binom{g}{3}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" linethickness="0pt"><mi>g</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}^{2g+2{\binom{g}{2}}+{\binom{g}{3}}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover:</span></p>

stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}[\mathbf{t}_{S_{1},\alpha}]</annotation></semantics></math> acts on <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" <p id="S4.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The result for general <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is more complicated, so we omit the explicit description. However we note the following.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.ThmDef10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.ThmDef10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 4.10</span></span><span id="S4.ThmDef10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.ThmDef10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{K}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{K}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> be the rank <math id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> free abelian group generated by <math id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S_{k}\#S_{k},\alpha}-8\mathbf{t}_{S_{k},\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{t}_{S_{k}\#S_{k},\alpha}-8\mathbf{t}_{S_{k},\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq g</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{K}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{K}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is the subgroup of <math id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> consisting of all diffeomorphisms that act trivially on <math id="S4.ThmDef10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Clearly <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{K}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{K}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> acts trivially on <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. Now suppose <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is a diffeomorphism acting trivially on <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. By Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef7" title="Lemma 4.7. ‣ 4.2.2. The cup product of 𝐻^∗((∨_𝑔(𝑆^2∨𝑆^3))_𝑓) ‣ 4.2. The cubic form ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.7</span></a> the cubic form on <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{2}({(M_{g})}_{f})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{2}({(M_{g})}_{f})</annotation></semantics></math> is zero, thus <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\nu_{f}}_{*}([{(M_{g})}_{f}])=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>ν</mi><mi>f</mi><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\nu_{f}}_{*}([{(M_{g})}_{f}])=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> lies in <math id="S4.SS3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{K}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{K}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>

<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5. </span>Torelli groups of spin 5-manifolds</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Throughout this section <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> will denote a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold unless otherwise stated. We compute the Torelli group of <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> has no 2-torsion, determine the generators, and prove Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a>, using Kreck’s modified surgery theory.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1. </span>The mapping class group of <math id="S5.SS1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As the first step we compute the relative mapping class group <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>-fold boundary connected sum of <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times D^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times D^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Note that <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M_{g}={\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\cup_{id}\overline{{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}={\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\cup_{id}\overline{{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})}</annotation></semantics></math> is a twisted double, thus there is a well-defined homomorphism</p>
<table id="S5.Ex194" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex194.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">given by extending a diffeomorphism of <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> by the identity map on the second copy of <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>. This homomorphism is surjective, since by Theorem <a href="#S4.ThmDef9" title="Theorem 4.9. ‣ 4.3. The group ℐ(𝑀_𝑔) ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.9</span></a> <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is generated by Dehn twists about certain embeddings of <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> which, up to isotopy, are supported in <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>. This proves the following.</p>

stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\overline{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math> to itself. By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Theorem 3]</cite>, this is true if and only if the modified surgery obstruction <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is elementary (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Page 730]</cite> for definition), which lies in the monoid <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l_{6}^{\sim}(e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mn>6</mn><mo>∼</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l_{6}^{\sim}(e)</annotation></semantics></math> since the image of the universal Stiefel–Whitney class <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{4}\in H^{4}(B\mathrm{SO};\mathbb{Z}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>SO</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{4}\in H^{4}(B\mathrm{SO};\mathbb{Z}/2)</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{4}(B\mathrm{Spin};\mathbb{Z}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Spin</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation We show that <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes, thus is elementary. In fact, by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre85</a>, Theorem 5.2 (b)]</cite>, <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> lies in a certain abelian group <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>L</mi><mn>6</mn><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)</annotation></semantics></math>. By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre85</a>, Lemma 4.1]</cite> and the fact that the Whitehead group of the trivial group is trivial, there is a surjective homomorphism <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{6}(\mathbb{Z})\rightarrow L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>L</mi><mn>6</mn><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{6}(\mathbb{Z})\rightarrow L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>L</mi><mn>6</mn><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>L</mi><mn>6</mn><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{6}^{s,\tau}(e,\mathbb{Z}e)</annotation></semantics></math> is nontrivial, then it is isomorphic to <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{6}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{6}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> and the nontrivial element is detected by the Arf–Kervaire invariant <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wal99</a>]</cite>. Since <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> admits a framing with nontrivial Kervaire invariant, we may form a connected sum of <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> (the trace of this connected sum operation is a normal <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-bordism relative to boundary) which has vanishing modified surgery obstruction, if <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is a bordism invariant it must vanish.</span></p>

stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ν</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W^{\prime},\nu^{\prime})=({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\times I,\overline{\nu}\times I)\sqcup(N^{\prime},\nu^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>. The corresponding <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordisms are thus normal <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-bordant and we denote the normal <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-bordism between them by <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(V,\tilde{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(V,\tilde{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math>. After smoothing the corners we may view <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> as a compact 7-manifold with boundary given by gluing the two <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordisms (which are both homotopy equivalent to <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>) along the boundary via the identity map, and by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Corollary 1]</cite> we may assume that the normal <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-structures of these <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordisms are 3-connected. By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Theorem 5]</cite> we can assume that the modified surgery obstruction <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(V,\tilde{\nu})\in l_{7}^{\sim}(e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mn>7</mn><mo>∼</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(V,\tilde{\nu})\in l_{7}^{\sim}(e)</annotation></semantics></math> is elementary, thus by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Theorem 4]</cite> we can assume that <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(V,\tilde{\nu})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(V,\tilde{\nu})</annotation></semantics></math> is an <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordism relative to boundary. The <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordism theorem then implies that the diffeomorphisms given by <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N^{\prime},\nu^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ν</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N^{\prime},\nu^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> are pseudoisotopic relative to boundary, and hence are isotopic relative to boundary by Cerf’s pseudoisotopy theorem. Therefore our construction yields a well-defined map <math id="S5.SS1.p6.m27" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\Phi:{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi:{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 5.3</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the proof of Lemma <a href="#S5.ThmDef2" title="Lemma 5.2. ‣ 5.1. The mapping class group of (♮^𝑔(𝑆^2×𝐷^3),∂) ‣ 5. Torelli groups of spin 5-manifolds ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> we used the unpublished work of Kreck <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre85</a>]</cite> to show that the surgery obstruction <math id="S5.ThmDef3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes. In fact it suffices to show that <math id="S5.ThmDef3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is elementary, and this can be proved directly without using <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre85</a>]</cite>. We present such a proof in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A A direct proof of the claim that 𝜃(𝑊,𝜈) is elementary ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5.4</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The map <math id="S5.ThmDef4.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\Phi:{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℂ</mi><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi:{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)</annotation></semantics></math> is a surjective homomorphism.</span></p>
</div>

<p id="S5.SS1.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text">is normal <math id="S5.SS1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-bordant, relative to boundary, to the result of gluing the two <math id="S5.SS1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>-cobordisms along <math id="S5.SS1.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\times\{1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\times\{1\}</annotation></semantics></math> via the identity map. rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>I</mi><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation I)\cup\bigl((\overline{\nu}\circ f)\times I\bigr)\Bigr).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS1.p8.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p8.9.1" class="ltx_text">Thus <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi([{(M_{g})}_{f},\tilde{H}])=[f]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi([{(M_{g})}_{f},\tilde{H}])=[f]</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence <math id="S5.SS1.p8.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi</annotation></semantics></math> is surjective.
∎</span></p>
</div>

<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2. </span>Extending diffeomorphisms by identity</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">According to Barden’s construction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bar65</a>, Theorem 2.3]</cite>, a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is a twisted double of a boundary connected sum of <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times D^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times D^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. the fundamental classes of the embedded spheres <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}(S^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo <div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The main result of this section is the following.</p>

<div id="S5.ThmDef6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Thm">

<p id="S5.ThmDef6.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef6.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is an isomorphism, and the homomorphism <math id="S5.ThmDef6.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g+2s}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g+2s}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is surjective.</span></p>

<div id="S5.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">By Proposition <a href="#S3.ThmDef6" title="Proposition 3.6. ‣ 3.3. The canonical quotient homomorphism ‣ 3. The spin bordism groups of certain Eilenberg–MacLane spaces ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.6</span></a> it suffices to show that the diagram commutes. Namely, let <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> be a diffeomorphism representing an element of <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g+2s}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}({\natural}^{g+2s}(S^{2}\times D^{3}),\partial)</annotation></semantics></math>, still denote its image in <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g+2s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g+2s})</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and denote its image in <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation <p id="S5.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">So the isomorphism type of <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is determined for <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology. Furthermore, the commutative diagrams in Theorem <a href="#S5.ThmDef6" title="Theorem 5.6. ‣ 5.2. Extending diffeomorphisms by identity ‣ 5. Torelli groups of spin 5-manifolds ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a> and in the proof of Proposition <a href="#S3.ThmDef6" title="Proposition 3.6. ‣ 3.3. We summarize the results into the following theorem, whose proof is a straightforward verification.</p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 5.7</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> isomorphic to the group described in (<a href="#S5.Ex234" title="5.3. Assume in addition that <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>. For brevity, suppose an integer <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g+2(s_{1}+\cdots+s_{i-1})+1\leq k\leq g+2(s_{1}+\cdots+s_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g+2(s_{1}+\cdots+s_{i-1})+1\leq k\leq g+2(s_{1}+\cdots+s_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, denote</span></p>

<p id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">and write <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\Delta_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\Delta_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq g</annotation></semantics></math>, write <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\Delta_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\Delta_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math>. In the following we always assume <math id="S5.ThmDef7.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k&lt;l&lt;h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k&lt;l&lt;h</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4. </span>The group extension and the action of <math id="S5.SS4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S5.SS4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We are at the position to complete the proof of Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. <div id="S5.ThmDef8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is a short exact sequence of groups</span></p>
