<div id="S5.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The first part of Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a> is a special case of this theorem. To study this extension problem the following action of <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M},w_{2}(M))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M},w_{2}(M))</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is crucial (see for example <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bro82</a>, Chapter IV]</cite>). Let <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M},w_{2}(M))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M},w_{2}(M))</annotation></semantics></math> be an automorphism of <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> be an orientation preserving diffeomorphism such that <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{f_{h}}_{*}=h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>f</mi><mi>h</mi><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{f_{h}}_{*}=h</annotation></semantics></math>. The action of <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M},w_{2}(M))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M},w_{2}(M))</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is defined by</p>

<div id="S5.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In the remaining part of this subsection let <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology. For such <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> isotopy invariants of diffeomorphisms in <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> are defined, and the action of <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is thus calculable.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The Torelli group <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to the bordism group <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math>. Recall that in <a href="#S1.SS1" title="1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a> we defined the following <em id="S5.SS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">standard action</em> of <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math>. Given <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M),L_{M})</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{h}:K(H_{2}(M),2)\rightarrow K(H_{2}(M),2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{h}:K(H_{2}(M),2)\rightarrow K(H_{2}(M),2)</annotation></semantics></math> be the map inducing <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> on the second homology, which is unique up to homotopy. Then <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[N,\delta_{h}\circ\nu]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>ν</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[N,\delta_{h}\circ\nu]</annotation></semantics></math> is a well-defined bordism class in <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}(K(H_{2}(M),2))</annotation></semantics></math> and the standard action is defined by <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\cdot[N,\nu]\coloneqq[N,\delta_{h}\circ\nu]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>ν</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\cdot[N,\nu]\coloneqq[N,\delta_{h}\circ\nu]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<div id="S5.SS4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S5.SS4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">It suffices to show that <math id="S5.SS4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(h\cdot[f])=h\cdot\rho([f])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(h\cdot[f])=h\cdot\rho([f])</annotation></semantics></math>, namely</span></p>
<table id="S5.Ex245" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS4.p6.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.p6.6.1" class="ltx_text">Thus <math id="S5.SS4.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[M_{h\cdot f},\nu_{h\cdot f}]=[M_{f},\delta_{h}\circ\nu_{f}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[M_{h\cdot f},\nu_{h\cdot f}]=[M_{f},\delta_{h}\circ\nu_{f}]</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<p id="S5.SS4.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The proof of Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. <h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 5.10</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wal63b</a>, Section 4]</cite> Wall gave a complete algebraic description of the linking form <math id="S5.ThmDef10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{M}</annotation></semantics></math>. <section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5. </span>Diffeomorphisms acting nontrivially on homology are not Dehn twists</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with no 2-torsion in homology. We show that a diffeomorphism of <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> acting nontrivially on <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is not isotopic to any Dehn twist. This is achieved by determining all possible Dehn twists of <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The normal bundle of an embedding <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{k}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{k}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math> is classified by its clutching function which is an element of <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{k-1}(\mathrm{SO}(5-k))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{k-1}(\mathrm{SO}(5-k))</annotation></semantics></math>, so it is trivial (when <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2</annotation></semantics></math>, use the fact that <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is spin). Thus for <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq 4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{k}\times D^{5-k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{k}\times D^{5-k}</annotation></semantics></math> embeds in <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> embeds in <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. Assume that this is the case and let <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S:S^{k}\times D^{5-k}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S:S^{k}\times D^{5-k}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math> be an embedding. To define a Dehn twist about <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> one needs to choose an element of <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{5-k}(\mathrm{SO}(k+1))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{5-k}(\mathrm{SO}(k+1))</annotation></semantics></math>, which is nontrivial only if <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2,4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2,4</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS5.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))\cong\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))\cong\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{1}(\mathrm{SO}(5))\cong\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{1}(\mathrm{SO}(5))\cong\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math>), so we have proved the following.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef11" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 5.11</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">A Dehn twist about an embedded 1-sphere or 3-sphere of a closed 5-manifold is isotopic to the identity.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">By Lemma <a href="#S4.ThmDef1" title="Lemma 4.1. ‣ 4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> a Dehn twist about an embedded 2-sphere lies in the Torelli group of <math id="S5.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. It remains to consider Dehn twists about embedded 4-spheres, which are of order 1 or 2 in <math id="S5.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> since <math id="S5.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{1}(\mathrm{SO}(5))\cong\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{1}(\mathrm{SO}(5))\cong\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S5.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=4</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S5.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is an embedding of <math id="S5.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{4}\times D^{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{4}\times D^{1}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S5.SS5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. A natural way to produce such an embedding is to realize it as the thickened meridian sphere of a 0-surgery (for example, the “neck” of a connected sum). In fact an embedding of <math id="S5.SS5.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S5.SS5.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> always arises in this way.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef12" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 5.12</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold, and let <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S:S^{4}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S:S^{4}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math> be an embedding. Then there are two simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds, such that <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is the connected sum of them, and <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(S^{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(S^{4})</annotation></semantics></math> is the meridian sphere of this connected sum operation. In particular, if <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is a prime number, then <math id="S5.ThmDef12.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(S^{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(S^{4})</annotation></semantics></math> is the boundary of an embedded 5-disc.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S5.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS5.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="S5.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(1))=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(1))=0</annotation></semantics></math> we may extend <math id="S5.SS5.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> to an embedding <math id="S5.SS5.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{4}\times D^{1}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{4}\times D^{1}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math>. We perform a surgery on this embedding and denote the resulting manifold by <math id="S5.SS5.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. The homology groups of <math id="S5.SS5.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> can be calculated using homology exact sequence of pairs and are as follows.</span></p>
</div>

<div id="S5.SS5.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS5.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Thus <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> has two path components. By Seifert–van Kampen theorem each component is a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold. Now <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is the connected sum of these two manifolds and <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(S^{4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(S^{4})</annotation></semantics></math> is the meridian sphere of this connected sum operation. If <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, by the classification of simply connected 5-manifolds <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sma62</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bar65</a>]</cite>, <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is diffeomorphic to <math id="S5.SS5.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\sqcup S^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⊔</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\sqcup S^{5}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef13" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef13.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 5.13</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef13.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef13.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Only the trivial element of <math id="S5.ThmDef13.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{4}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{4}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by an embedding of <math id="S5.ThmDef13.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef14" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 5.14</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef14.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef14.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S5.ThmDef14.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold, and let <math id="S5.ThmDef14.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S:S^{4}\times D^{1}\hookrightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S:S^{4}\times D^{1}\hookrightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math> be an embedding.</span></p>
<ul id="S5.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I2.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(1)</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.ix1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.ix1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.ix1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The Dehn twist about </span><math id="S5.I2.ix1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> acts trivially on </span><math id="S5.I2.ix1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(2)</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.ix2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If </span><math id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> has no 2-torsion, then the Dehn twist about </span><math id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is isotopic to </span><math id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.ix3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(3)</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.ix3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If </span><math id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is isomorphic to </span><math id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℤ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> or </span><math id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>p</mi><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/{p^{r}})}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, where </span><math id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is a prime number, then the Dehn twist about </span><math id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is isotopic to </span><math id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I2.ix3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S5.SS5.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS5.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">(1) and (2) are clear. To prove (3), note that this Dehn twist is supported in an embedded 5-disc, and thus its isotopy class lies in the image of <math id="S5.SS5.p7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(D^{5},\partial)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(D^{5},\partial)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S5.SS5.p7.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(D^{5},\partial)=\Theta_{6}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(D^{5},\partial)=\Theta_{6}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef15" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 5.15</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef15.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">All the Dehn twists of a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold <math id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> act trivially on <math id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> has no 2-torsion or is isomorphic to <math id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/{2^{r}})}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/{2^{r}})}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, then Dehn twists about embedded <math id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-spheres with <math id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\neq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\neq 2</annotation></semantics></math> are isotopic to <math id="S5.ThmDef15.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p8.1" class="ltx_p">We have seen in <a href="#S1.SS1" title="1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a> that the isotopy classes of Dehn twists about embedded 2-spheres are determined by elements of <math id="S5.SS5.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS5.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(3))</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus we have determined all possible Dehn twists of <math id="S5.SS5.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S5.SS5.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> has no 2-torsion or is isomorphic to <math id="S5.SS5.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/{2^{r}})}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/{2^{r}})}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.ThmDef16" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.ThmDef16.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 5.16</span></span><span id="S5.ThmDef16.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.ThmDef16.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.ThmDef16.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The results in this subsection are formulated for spin manifolds. They remain valid in the nonspin case after mild modification of the statements.</p>
</div>

<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6. </span>The mapping class group of <math id="S6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> and its abelianization</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section we focus on <math id="S6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. We show that <math id="S6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is a semi-direct product of <math id="S6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>, and compute the abelianization of <math id="S6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. We also determine <math id="S6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>, the <em id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">full</em> mapping class group of <math id="S6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1. </span>Splitting the group extension for <math id="S6.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that, given a short exact sequence of groups</p>
<table id="S6.Ex257" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex257.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\rightarrow A\rightarrow E\xrightarrow{\phi}Q\rightarrow 1" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>E</mi><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_italic" mathsize="0.700em" mathvariant="italic">ϕ</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\rightarrow A\rightarrow E\xrightarrow{\phi}Q\rightarrow 1</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> abelian, the group <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> acts on <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\cdot a=s(g)as(g)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\cdot a=s(g)as(g)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s:Q\rightarrow E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s:Q\rightarrow E</annotation></semantics></math> is a set theoretic cross section. This action is independent to the choice of <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> and is used to define the group structure of the semi-direct product <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A\rtimes Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋊</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A\rtimes Q</annotation></semantics></math> (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bro82</a>, Chapter IV]</cite>). We note the following.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.ThmDef1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.ThmDef1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 6.1</span></span><span id="S6.ThmDef1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S6.ThmDef1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.ThmDef1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.ThmDef1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If there is a map <math id="S6.ThmDef1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi:E\rightarrow A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi:E\rightarrow A</annotation></semantics></math> which restricts to identity on <math id="S6.ThmDef1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, and</span></p>
<table id="S6.Ex258" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex258.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi(g_{1}g_{2})=\chi(g_{1})+g_{1}\chi(g_{2})g_{1}^{-1}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi(g_{1}g_{2})=\chi(g_{1})+g_{1}\chi(g_{2})g_{1}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.ThmDef1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.ThmDef1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for <math id="S6.ThmDef1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{1},g_{2}\in E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{1},g_{2}\in E</annotation></semantics></math>, then the short exact sequence splits.</span></p>

<p id="S6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We call such a map <math id="S6.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>χ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi</annotation></semantics></math> a <em id="S6.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">crossed splitting</em>.</p>
</div>

The action of <math id="S6.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S6.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is described by Theorem <a href="#S5.ThmDef9" title="Theorem 5.9. ‣ 5.4. <div id="S6.ThmDef2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.ThmDef2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 6.2</span></span><span id="S6.ThmDef2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S6.ThmDef2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.ThmDef2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.ThmDef2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If <math id="S6.ThmDef2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[f]\in\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[f]\in\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S6.ThmDef2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi([f])=\rho([f])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi([f])=\rho([f])</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>

<p id="S6.SS1.p6.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p6.4.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> lies in the Torelli group, by our definition of <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\nu}_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\nu}_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> there is a map <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\nu}_{f}:V\rightarrow{(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>f</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\nu}_{f}:V\rightarrow{(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> extends <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\nu}_{f}\sqcup\nu_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>⊔</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\nu}_{f}\sqcup\nu_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> up to homotopy. By gluing collar neighborhoods to <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> if needed, we obtain the desired normal <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-bordism between <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X_{f},\tilde{\nu}_{f})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X_{f},\tilde{\nu}_{f})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS1.p6.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="({(M_{g})}_{f},\nu_{f})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">({(M_{g})}_{f},\nu_{f})</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.ThmDef3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 6.3</span></span><span id="S6.ThmDef3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S6.ThmDef3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.ThmDef3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.ThmDef3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The map <math id="S6.ThmDef3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi:\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})\rightarrow{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>6</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℙ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi:\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})\rightarrow{\Omega}^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{6}((\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is a crossed splitting.</span></p>
</div>

<div id="S6.SS1.4" class="ltx_proof">

<p id="S6.SS1.p8.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS1.p8.5.1" class="ltx_text">Clearly <math id="S6.SS1.p8.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is a simply connected bordism between <math id="S6.SS1.p8.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{f}\sqcup X_{f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>⊔</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{f}\sqcup X_{f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS1.p8.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{f\circ f^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{f\circ f^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Using Mayer–Vietoris sequence we see that <math id="S6.SS1.p8.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is spin. Then the spin structure of <math id="S6.SS1.p8.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is unique and thus <math id="S6.SS1.p8.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is a spin bordism.</span></p>

<div id="S6.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Therefore <math id="S6.SS1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})\cong\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rtimes\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋊</mo><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})\cong\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\rtimes\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover, let <math id="S6.SS1.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Top}^{+}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Top</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Top}^{+}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> be the topological group of orientation preserving homeomorphisms of an oriented manifold <math id="S6.SS1.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S6.SS1.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G^{+}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>G</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G^{+}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> be the topological monoid of orientation preserving homotopy equivalences of <math id="S6.SS1.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, both equipped with compact-open topology. <p id="S6.SS1.p11.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S6.SS1.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> not necessarily an abelian group, we say that this short exact sequence <em id="S6.SS1.p11.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">splits</em> if there is a group theoretic cross section, namely a homomorphism <math id="S6.SS1.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s:Q\rightarrow E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s:Q\rightarrow E</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S6.SS1.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi\circ s=id_{Q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi\circ s=id_{Q}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">By Theorem <a href="#S6.ThmDef4" title="Theorem 6.4. ‣ 6.1. Splitting the group extension for 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ 6. The mapping class group of 𝑀_𝑔 and its abelianization ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.4</span></a> the group structure of <math id="S6.SS1.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> is determined. This completes the proof of Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef2" title="Theorem 1.2. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a>.</p>

<div id="S6.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">

<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof is a straightforward calculation using the action of <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> determined in Theorem <a href="#S5.ThmDef9" title="Theorem 5.9. ‣ 5.4. For <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=1</annotation></semantics></math> the result is clear. For <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, since <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})\cong\mathbb{Z}^{g}\oplus H_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo>⊕</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> acts on the <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> summand in the standard way (this follows from the definition of the bordism invariants), we have <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathcal{I}(M_{g})}_{\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})}={(H_{g})}_{\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{I}(M_{g})}_{\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})}={(H_{g})}_{\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})}</annotation></semantics></math>. Recall that the general linear group <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> is generated by the (block) diagonal matrices (where the empty entries are 1 on the diagonal and 0 otherwise)</span></p>
