<p id="S6.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">It suffices to check the action of these matrices on the generators of <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, which can be calculated using the universal coefficient theorem.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=2,3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=2,3</annotation></semantics></math> we see that the generators <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2(x_{k}^{2}x_{l})^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(x_{k}^{2}x_{l})^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> are zero in the coinvariant, and the remaining generators are mapped to the same element, which is of order at most 2, in the coinvariant. Thus the coinvariant for <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=2,3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=2,3</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math>. Consider the homomorphism <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{g}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{g}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math> defined by adding the coordinates except those correspond to the generators <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2(x_{k}^{2}x_{l})^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(x_{k}^{2}x_{l})^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>. By checking on the generators of <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> we see that this is a surjective homomorphism which is invariant under the action of <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>, thus it induces a surjection from the coinvariant to <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math>, it follows that the coinvariant is <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=2,3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=2,3</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math> the aforementioned effects on the generators of <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> are still true, namely, <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2(x_{k}^{2}x_{l})^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(x_{k}^{2}x_{l})^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> are zero in the coinvariant, and the remaining generators (including <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{k}x_{l}x_{h})^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{k}x_{l}x_{h})^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>) are mapped to the same element, which is of order at most 2, in the coinvariant. Moreover, the generators <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{k}x_{l}x_{h})^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{k}x_{l}x_{h})^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> are mapped to zero, which force all generators of <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> to be zero in the coinvariant. Thus the coinvariant is trivial for <math id="S6.SS2.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Corollary <a href="#S1.ThmDef6" title="Corollary 1.6. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.6</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="S6.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Part (1) is evident. Part (2) follows from the well-known fact that given a topological group <math id="S6.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math>, one has <math id="S6.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{1}(BG)\cong\pi_{0}(G)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{1}(BG)\cong\pi_{0}(G)</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore <math id="S6.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{1}(BG)\cong H_{1}(\pi_{0}(G))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{1}(BG)\cong H_{1}(\pi_{0}(G))</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3. </span>The full mapping class group of <math id="S6.SS3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Barden’s theorem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bar65</a>, Theorem 2.2]</cite> implies that for each simply connected closed 5-manifold <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> there is an exact sequence</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.Ex295.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(M)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2\rightarrow 1," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(M)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2\rightarrow 1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S6.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(M)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(M)\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math> maps an isotopy class to its degree. Whether this exact sequence splits or not is unknown in general. For <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> a (group theoretic) cross section <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/2\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/2\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is provided by the orientation reversing diffeomorphism <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r:S^{2}\times S^{3}\rightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r:S^{2}\times S^{3}\rightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> defined as <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the antipodal map. As a generalization of Corollary <a href="#S1.ThmDef3" title="Corollary 1.3. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.3</span></a> we have the following computation of <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S6.ThmDef8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 6.8</span></span><span id="S6.ThmDef8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S6.ThmDef8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.ThmDef8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.ThmDef8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The full mapping class group <math id="S6.ThmDef8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> has the following presentation:</span></p>

<p id="S6.ThmDef8.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.ThmDef8.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S6.ThmDef8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" respectively.</span></p>

<div id="S6.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">

<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7. </span>Stabilization of <math id="S7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math></h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section <math id="S7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a simply connected closed spin manifold with no 2-torsion in homology. We study the stabilization of <math id="S7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to connected sum with <math id="S7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\subset M</annotation></semantics></math> be an embedded 5-disc, and let <math id="S7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W\coloneqq M\setminus\mathring{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W\coloneqq M\setminus\mathring{D}</annotation></semantics></math> be the compact 5-manifold obtained by digging out the interior of <math id="S7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. <p id="S7.p1.6" class="ltx_p">We call these homomorphisms the <em id="S7.p1.6.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">stabilization maps</em>. Two orientation preserving diffeomorphisms of <math id="S7.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> are <em id="S7.p1.6.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">stably isotopic</em> if their isotopy classes are mapped to the same element by a composition of stabilization maps. Denote <math id="S7.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}(M\#M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}(M\#M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M\#M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M\#M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S7.p1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}_{g}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>MCG</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}_{g}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.p1.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}_{g}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}_{g}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> respectively. <p id="S7.p1.7" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S7.p1.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M)\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{g},L_{M})\rightarrow\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M)\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{g+1},L_{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>Aut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M)\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{g},L_{M})\rightarrow\mathrm{Aut}(H_{2}(M)\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{g+1},L_{M})</annotation></semantics></math> is given by taking direct sum with <math id="S7.p1.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id:\mathbb{Z}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id:\mathbb{Z}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>. This is clearly injective for each <math id="S7.p1.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>. By the computation of <math id="S7.p1.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> we see that the stabilization map <math id="S7.p1.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}_{g}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}_{g+1}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}_{g}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}_{g+1}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is injective for each <math id="S7.p1.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, thus the stabilization map <math id="S7.p1.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}_{g}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}_{g+1}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>MCG</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>MCG</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}_{g}(M)\rightarrow\mathrm{MCG}_{g+1}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is injective for each <math id="S7.p1.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>. In other words, two orientation preserving diffeomorphisms of <math id="S7.p1.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> are not stably isotopic if they are not isotopic. This proves Corollary <a href="#S1.ThmDef7" title="Corollary 1.7. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.7</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<p id="S7.p2.2" class="ltx_p">By Lemma <a href="#S6.ThmDef7" title="Lemma 6.7. ‣ 6.2. The abelianization of MCG(𝑀_𝑔) ‣ 6. The mapping class group of 𝑀_𝑔 and its abelianization ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.7</span></a>, <math id="S7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{*}:H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g}))\rightarrow H_{1}(\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{*}:H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g}))\rightarrow H_{1}(\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z}))</annotation></semantics></math> is an isomorphism for <math id="S7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>. By the homological stability of <math id="S7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cha80</a>, Theorem 3.2]</cite>, the stabilization map induces an isomorphism <math id="S7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{1}(\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z}))\cong H_{1}(\mathrm{GL}_{g+1}(\mathbb{Z}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>GL</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℤ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{1}(\mathrm{GL}_{g}(\mathbb{Z}))\cong H_{1}(\mathrm{GL}_{g+1}(\mathbb{Z}))</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S7.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, for <math id="S7.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>, the stabilization map induces an isomorphism</p>
<table id="S7.Ex309" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex309.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g}))\xrightarrow{\cong}H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g+1}))." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">≅</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>MCG</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g}))\xrightarrow{\cong}H_{1}(\mathrm{MCG}(M_{g+1})).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S7.p2.3" class="ltx_p">This proves Corollary <a href="#S1.ThmDef8" title="Corollary 1.8. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.8</span></a>.</p>

<div id="S7.ThmDef1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S7.ThmDef1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 7.1</span></span><span id="S7.ThmDef1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S7.ThmDef1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.ThmDef1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S7.ThmDef1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}\coloneqq M_{g}\setminus\mathring{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}\coloneqq M_{g}\setminus\mathring{D}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then one can define the stabilization map for relative diffeomorphism groups</p>
<table id="S7.Ex310" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S7.ThmDef1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which induces a stabilization map on the classifying spaces</p>

<p id="S7.ThmDef1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The homological stability of <math id="S7.ThmDef1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="B\mathrm{Diff}(W_{g},\partial)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>Diff</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\mathrm{Diff}(W_{g},\partial)</annotation></semantics></math> under the stabilization map is an important topic in geometric topology (see for example <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx32" title="" class="ltx_ref">MW07</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx15" title="" class="ltx_ref">GRW18</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx14" title="" class="ltx_ref">GRW17</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Per16a</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Per16b</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx12" title="" class="ltx_ref">ER24</a>]</cite>). For dimension 5 the homological stability result has not been established. Our result shows that <math id="S7.ThmDef1.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H_{1}(B\mathrm{Diff}(W_{g},\partial))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>Diff</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo>∂</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{1}(B\mathrm{Diff}(W_{g},\partial))</annotation></semantics></math> stabilizes under the stabilization map when <math id="S7.ThmDef1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>

Similarly <math id="S7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}_{\infty}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}_{\infty}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is called the <em id="S7.p3.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">stable Torelli group</em> of <math id="S7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. The following result is evident.</p>

<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8. </span>Homotopy equivalences of <math id="S8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math></h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section <math id="S8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with no 2-torsion in homology, unless otherwise specified. We compare diffeomorphisms and homotopy equivalences of <math id="S8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> using the forgetful homomorphism <math id="S8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi:\mathcal{I}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi:\mathcal{I}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>. To formulate the main result of this section we need to recall some previous works.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The homotopy Torelli group has a subgroup <math id="S8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>haut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>M</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})</annotation></semantics></math> consisting of elements which can be represented by homotopy equivalences restricting to the identity map on the complement of the interior of a fixed 5-cell. This group was completely computed by Baues and Buth in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx3" title="" class="ltx_ref">BB96</a>, Theorem B]</cite>. Moreover, in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx3" title="" class="ltx_ref">BB96</a>]</cite> Baues–Buth made an extensive investigation of the (unoriented) homotopy automorphism group of <math id="S8.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. In particular, in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx3" title="" class="ltx_ref">BB96</a>, page 581]</cite> they defined a homomorphism</p>
<table id="S8.Ex317" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S8.p2.2" class="ltx_p">which is a homotopic version of the mapping torus construction <math id="S8.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> defined in Section <a href="#S2" title="2. We denote the image of <math id="S8.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S8.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{M}^{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>h</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{M}^{h}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We also recall that Stöcker has proved that there is a bijection <math id="S8.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(M)\rightarrow H_{3}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(M)\rightarrow H_{3}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stö82</a>, Theorem 1.2]</cite>, where <math id="S8.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is the surgery structure set of <math id="S8.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p4.1" class="ltx_p">From now on we suppose <math id="S8.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> has the isomorphism type of (<a href="#S5.Ex234" title="5.3. For such <math id="S8.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> the aforementioned results of Baues–Buth and Stöcker can be stated as follows.</p>

<div id="S8.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The main result of this section is the following.</p>

<div id="S8.ThmDef4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.ThmDef4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 8.4</span></span><span id="S8.ThmDef4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.ThmDef4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology, then there is a commutative diagram of exact sequences (of based sets at <math id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, of groups at other terms)</span></p>

<p id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where the based map <math id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{S}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)\rightarrow\mathcal{S}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> maps a homotopy class <math id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[f]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[f]</annotation></semantics></math> to the homotopy smoothing <math id="S8.ThmDef4.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[f:M\rightarrow M]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[f:M\rightarrow M]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="S8.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef9" title="Theorem 1.9. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.9</span></a> follows from Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef4" title="Theorem 8.4. ‣ 8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a> as a special case. Before presenting the proof of Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef4" title="Theorem 8.4. ‣ 8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a> we elaborate this theorem by some remarks (in which <math id="S8.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is assumed to satisfy the conditions in Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef4" title="Theorem 8.4. ‣ 8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.ThmDef5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.ThmDef5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 8.5</span></span><span id="S8.ThmDef5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.ThmDef5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.ThmDef5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef4" title="Theorem 8.4. ‣ 8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a> <math id="S8.ThmDef5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is the group of isotopy classes of diffeomorphisms of <math id="S8.ThmDef5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> that are homotopic to <math id="S8.ThmDef5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="id_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">id_{M}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is (abstractly) isomorphic to <math id="S8.ThmDef5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> and we have given explicit constructions of its generators. A result of Browder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bro67</a>, Theorem 6]</cite> implies that such group of a simply connected closed 5-manifold with positive second Betti number contains a free cyclic subgroup. Our computation of <math id="S8.ThmDef5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K(M)</annotation></semantics></math> can be viewed as a supplement of Browder’s result in dimension 5.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.ThmDef6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.ThmDef6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 8.6</span></span><span id="S8.ThmDef6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.ThmDef6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By our computation of <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, the left vertical short exact sequence in the diagram splits, thus so does the right vertical short exact sequence. Thus the homotopy Torelli group <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is a semi-direct product of <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>haut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>M</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{M}</annotation></semantics></math>. The action of <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> on the elements of <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>haut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>M</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})</annotation></semantics></math> that cannot be represented by diffeomorphisms is unknown, so the group structure of <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}^{h}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> (for example, whether it is abelian) is unknown. For <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, the homotopy Torelli group <math id="S8.ThmDef6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}^{h}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}^{h}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is not abelian (<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Saw75</a>]</cite>, see Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef9" title="Theorem 8.9 (Sawashita). ‣ 8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.9</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.ThmDef7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.ThmDef7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 8.7</span></span><span id="S8.ThmDef7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.ThmDef7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.ThmDef7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">According to Baues (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx3" title="" class="ltx_ref">BB96</a>, page 580]</cite>) there is a surjective homomorphism</p>

<p id="S8.ThmDef7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">mapping a homotopy class, represented by a map <math id="S8.ThmDef7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma:S^{5}\rightarrow M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma:S^{5}\rightarrow M</annotation></semantics></math>, to the homotopy class of the homotopy equivalence</p>

<p id="S8.ThmDef7.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S8.ThmDef7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\rightarrow M\vee S^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∨</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\rightarrow M\vee S^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> is the quotient map collapsing the boundary of the 5-cell to a point. In fact <math id="S8.ThmDef7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> can be chosen to factor through the 4-skeleton of <math id="S8.ThmDef7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. Combining with Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef4" title="Theorem 8.4. ‣ 8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a>, this shows that each of the diffeomorphisms</p>

<p id="S8.p9.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p9.3.1" class="ltx_text">and the map <math id="S8.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})/{\mathrm{im}(\psi)}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>haut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>M</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>im</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})/{\mathrm{im}(\psi)}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is also injective. By Baues–Buth’s result (Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef1" title="Theorem 8.1 (Baues–Buth). ‣ 8. Thus the upper horizontal exact sequence induces the following exact sequence</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.p9.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.p9.5.1" class="ltx_text">This implies that <math id="S8.p9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2g}/{\psi(\mathbb{Z}^{g})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2g}/{\psi(\mathbb{Z}^{g})}</annotation></semantics></math> has at least <math id="S8.p9.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>g</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> elements. Since <math id="S8.p9.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2g}/{\psi(\mathbb{Z}^{g})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{2g}/{\psi(\mathbb{Z}^{g})}</annotation></semantics></math> admits an injection to <math id="S8.p9.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/2)}^{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, it contains precisely <math id="S8.p9.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>g</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{g}</annotation></semantics></math> elements, and <math id="S8.p9.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})\rightarrow\mathcal{S}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>haut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>M</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{haut}(M|\dot{M})\rightarrow\mathcal{S}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is surjective. Consequently we have <math id="S8.p9.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ker(\psi)=K(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ker</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ker(\psi)=K(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S8.p9.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> is equal to <math id="S8.p9.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{M}^{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>h</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{M}^{h}</annotation></semantics></math>. The proof is completed.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.ThmDef8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Rmk">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.ThmDef8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 8.8</span></span><span id="S8.ThmDef8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.ThmDef8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> has nontrivial 3-torsion in homology, we still have the commutative diagram in the proof of Theorem <a href="#S8.ThmDef4" title="Theorem 8.4. ‣ 8. Homotopy equivalences of 𝑀 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a>. It follows that <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{K}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{K}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> has nontrivial 3-torsion. For instance, if <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{K}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{K}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> is isomorphic to <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. This implies that the differential <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{4}_{7,0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{4}_{7,0}</annotation></semantics></math> of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence of <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{*}(K({(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2},2))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>∗</mo><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{*}(K({(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2},2))</annotation></semantics></math> is trivial. Consequently, we have <math id="S8.ThmDef8.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{7}(K({(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2},2))\cong H_{7}(K({(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2},2))\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>7</mn><mi>Spin</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{\mathrm{Spin}}_{7}(K({(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2},2))\cong H_{7}(K({(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{2},2))\cong{(\mathbb{Z}/3)}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p10.1" class="ltx_p">We close this section by discussing the case <math id="S8.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, where we can use Sawashita’s work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Saw75</a>]</cite> to obtain more concrete information about the group <math id="S8.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{haut}(S^{2}\times S^{3}|\dot{S^{2}\times S^{3}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>haut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{haut}(S^{2}\times S^{3}|\dot{S^{2}\times S^{3}})</annotation></semantics></math>. We will need the following result of Sawashita which is extracted from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Saw75</a>, Proposition 2.4, Theorem 2.6, Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.3]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.ThmDef9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_Thm">

<div id="S8.ThmDef9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.ThmDef9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.ThmDef9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given a space <math id="S8.ThmDef9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S8.ThmDef9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}^{h}(X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mi>h</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}^{h}(X)</annotation></semantics></math> be the group of homotopy classes of homotopy equivalences of <math id="S8.ThmDef9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> that act trivially on <math id="S8.ThmDef9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(X)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> is abelian, <math id="S8.p11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S_{1},\alpha}" display="inline" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S_{1}\#S_{1},\alpha}-8\mathbf{t}_{S_{1},\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" alttext="\mathbf{t}_{S_{1}\#S_{1},\alpha}-8\mathbf{t}_{S_{1},\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐭</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" alttext="\pi_{5}(S^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{5}(S^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> via the isomorphism</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex338.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{5}(S^{2})\oplus\pi_{5}(S^{3})=\pi_{5}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\cong\mathrm{haut}(S^{2}\times S^{3}|\dot{S^{2}\times S^{3}})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mi>haut</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{5}(S^{2})\oplus\pi_{5}(S^{3})=\pi_{5}(S^{2}\times S^{3})\cong\mathrm{haut}(S^{2}\times S^{3}|\dot{S^{2}\times S^{3}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
