<p id="S8.p11.2" class="ltx_p">It follows that the homotopy equivalences defined by the homotopy classes <math id="S8.p11.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,1),(1,1)\in\pi_{5}(S^{2})\oplus\pi_{5}(S^{3})=\mathbb{Z}/2\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,1),(1,1)\in\pi_{5}(S^{2})\oplus\pi_{5}(S^{3})=\mathbb{Z}/2\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2</annotation></semantics></math> are not homotopic to any diffeomorphism of <math id="S8.p11.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S9" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">9. </span>Embeddings of <math id="S9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math></h2>

<div id="S9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section we prove Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef10" title="Theorem 1.10. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.10</span></a> and Corollary <a href="#S1.ThmDef11" title="Corollary 1.11. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.11</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S1.ThmDef10" title="Theorem 1.10. ‣ 1.1. The results ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.10</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="S9.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">In Section <a href="#S4" title="4. The Torelli group of 𝑀_𝑔 ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> we determined the action of <math id="S9.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S9.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S9.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=1</annotation></semantics></math>, combining this with the computation of <math id="S9.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3. The full mapping class group of 𝑆^2×𝑆^3 ‣ 6. The mapping class group of 𝑀_𝑔 and its abelianization ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>, we see that a homotopy class <math id="S9.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a[S_{1}\circ\eta]+b[T_{1}]\in\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})=\mathbb{Z}[S_{1}\circ\eta]\oplus\mathbb{Z}[T_{1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊕</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a[S_{1}\circ\eta]+b[T_{1}]\in\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})=\mathbb{Z}[S_{1}\circ\eta]\oplus\mathbb{Z}[T_{1}]</annotation></semantics></math> (denoted by <math id="S9.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math> for simplicity) can be represented by <math id="S9.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\circ T_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\circ T_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> for some diffeomorphism <math id="S9.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f\in\mathrm{Diff}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>Diff</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f\in\mathrm{Diff}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> if and only if <math id="S9.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|b\right|=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|b\right|=1</annotation></semantics></math>. This proves (1).</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S9.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now we prove (2). We shall prove a slightly more general result relating embeddings of <math id="S9.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S9.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> to closed 5-manifolds with certain homology. Assume a homotopy class <math id="S9.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by an embedding of <math id="S9.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S9.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S9.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{2}(\mathrm{SO}(2))=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{2}(\mathrm{SO}(2))=0</annotation></semantics></math>, the normal bundle of this embedding is trivial, so there is an embedding <math id="S9.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{\prime}:S^{3}\times D^{2}\hookrightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{\prime}:S^{3}\times D^{2}\hookrightarrow S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> extending it. (This extension is in fact unique up to isotopy since <math id="S9.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(2))=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>SO</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(\mathrm{SO}(2))=0</annotation></semantics></math>.) We perform a surgery on <math id="S9.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>T</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> and denote the resulting closed spin 5-manifold by <math id="S9.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. Using Seifert–van Kampen theorem, Lefschetz duality and homology exact sequence of pairs, we see that <math id="S9.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{1}(M^{\prime})\cong\mathbb{Z}/{\left|b\right|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{1}(M^{\prime})\cong\mathbb{Z}/{\left|b\right|}</annotation></semantics></math> and the homology groups of <math id="S9.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> are given as follows.</span></p>

<div id="S9.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Conversely, let <math id="S9.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> be a closed spin 5-manifold with such homology and fundamental group. Choose a generator of <math id="S9.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{1}(M^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{1}(M^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>, it can be represented by an embedding <math id="S9.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{1}\times D^{4}\hookrightarrow M^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↪</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{1}\times D^{4}\hookrightarrow M^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, and we perform a surgery on this embedding. The resulting manifold is a simply connected closed spin 5-manifold with homology isomorphic to <math id="S9.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{*}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{*}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>, so by the classification of simply connected 5-manifolds <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sma62</a>, <a href="#bib.bibx2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bar65</a>]</cite> it is diffeomorphic to <math id="S9.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{2}\times S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{2}\times S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. The meridian sphere of this surgery represents an element of <math id="S9.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math id="S9.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S9.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,-b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,-b)</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S9.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\in\mathbb{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℤ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\in\mathbb{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>. By the computation of <math id="S9.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>MCG</mi><mo>±</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MCG}^{\pm}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>, the homotopy classes <math id="S9.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a+kb,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a+kb,b)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a+kb,-b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a+kb,-b)</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by embeddings of <math id="S9.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> for each integer <math id="S9.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S9.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|b\right|=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|b\right|=2</annotation></semantics></math> such a manifold is provided by the manifold <math id="S9.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> constructed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx16" title="" class="ltx_ref">GT98</a>, page 1168]</cite>, and for <math id="S9.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|b\right|\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|b\right|\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math> odd such a manifold is provided by a 5-dimensional lens space <math id="S9.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\left|b\right|}(\ell_{1},\ell_{2},\ell_{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo>|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>|</mo></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\left|b\right|}(\ell_{1},\ell_{2},\ell_{3})</annotation></semantics></math> (see for example <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hat02</a>, Example 2.43]</cite>). This proves (2).
∎</span></p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S9.ThmDef1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 9.1</span></span><span id="S9.ThmDef1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S9.ThmDef1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.ThmDef1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By a theorem of Whitney (see for example <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ran02</a>, page 169]</cite>), each element of <math id="S9.ThmDef1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(S^{2}\times S^{3})</annotation></semantics></math> can be represented by an immersion of <math id="S9.ThmDef1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>A direct proof of the claim that <math id="A1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is elementary</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the notations in the proof of Lemma <a href="#S5.ThmDef2" title="Lemma 5.2. ‣ 5.1. The mapping class group of (♮^𝑔(𝑆^2×𝐷^3),∂) ‣ 5. Torelli groups of spin 5-manifolds ‣ Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion in homology" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>. Write <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{0}={\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\times\{0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{0}={\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\times\{0\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{1}={\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\times\{1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">♮</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{1}={\natural}^{g}(S^{2}\times D^{3})\times\{1\}</annotation></semantics></math>. By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Corollary 1]</cite> we may assume that the normal <math id="A1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>-structure <math id="A1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu:W\rightarrow B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu:W\rightarrow B</annotation></semantics></math> is 3-connected. Now the obstruction <math id="A1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is represented by the following data</p>
<table id="A1.Ex340" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> is the intersection form on <math id="A1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> and the maps are Hurewicz homomorphisms (<math id="A1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mu}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mu}=0</annotation></semantics></math> since it maps into <math id="A1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{Z}/1=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ℤ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{Z}/1=0</annotation></semantics></math> by the definition of <math id="A1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l_{6}^{\sim}(e)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>l</mi><mn>6</mn><mo>∼</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l_{6}^{\sim}(e)</annotation></semantics></math>). Viewing <math id="A1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> as a simply connected compact 6-manifold with boundary <math id="A1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, we deduce from the homology exact sequence of <math id="A1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(W,M_{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W,M_{g})</annotation></semantics></math> that <math id="A1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> is free. The Hurewicz homomorphism <math id="A1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(W)\rightarrow H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(W)\rightarrow H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> is surjective (which can be seen from, for example, the homotopy exact sequence of <math id="A1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(W,N_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W,N_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>), thus <math id="A1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> is a direct summand of <math id="A1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math>. By Poincaré duality, <math id="A1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> is a skew-symmetric non-singular bilinear form on <math id="A1.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math>, thus <math id="A1.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> has a symplectic basis <math id="A1.p1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(e_{1},\cdots,e_{n},f_{1},\cdots,f_{n})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(e_{1},\cdots,e_{n},f_{1},\cdots,f_{n})</annotation></semantics></math>, such that the nonzero values of <math id="A1.p1.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> on them are</p>
<table id="A1.Ex343" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex343.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\lambda(e_{i},f_{i})=1,\quad\lambda(f_{i},e_{i})=-1,\quad i=1,\cdots,n." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(e_{i},f_{i})=1,\quad\lambda(f_{i},e_{i})=-1,\quad i=1,\cdots,n.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A1.p1.5" class="ltx_p">The rank <math id="A1.p1.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> free abelian group <math id="A1.p1.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>U</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U</annotation></semantics></math> generated by <math id="A1.p1.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{1},\cdots,e_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{1},\cdots,e_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> is a direct summand of <math id="A1.p1.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math>. View <math id="A1.p1.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>U</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U</annotation></semantics></math> as a direct summand of <math id="A1.p1.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="A1.p1.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{0}=U_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{0}=U_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> be the image of <math id="A1.p1.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>U</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U</annotation></semantics></math> under the Hurewicz homomorphism <math id="A1.p1.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{3}(W)\rightarrow H_{3}(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{3}(W)\rightarrow H_{3}(W)</annotation></semantics></math>. One checks that <math id="A1.p1.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>U</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.p1.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy the conditions in the definition in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bibx24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kre99</a>, Page 730]</cite>, proving that <math id="A1.p1.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(W,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(W,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> is elementary.</p>
